#1979. “Grim Reading” West Ham’s London Stadium Financial Problem Just Got Worse

West Ham supporters hoping that relegation to the Championship might bring some financial relief to the London Stadium’s troubled finances may be in for a shock.

The latest accounts for London Stadium LLP, covering the year ending March 2026, reveal an operation still struggling financially, with annual losses of £20.6m, negative net assets of almost £247m and a staggering £243.7m provision for expected losses under its long-term contractual arrangements.

While the figures represent an improvement on the previous year, the stadium remains heavily dependent on financial support from the Greater London Authority and, ultimately, London taxpayers.

But perhaps the most significant revelation for Hammers supporters is the financial impact of relegation.

The biggest concern in the accounts is an onerous contract provision of £243.7m.

In simple terms, this represents the stadium operator’s estimate of future losses from its long-term contractual commitments, principally its concession agreement with West Ham and its access agreement with UK Athletics.

The provision has increased from £206.7m in March 2024 to £241.5m in March 2025 and now £243.7m.

It is not a bill that needs paying immediately, but it highlights the scale of the financial challenge facing the stadium.

The London Stadium financial figures make for grim reading

The accounts explicitly acknowledge the financial consequences of West Ham dropping out of the Premier League.

The stadium’s financial forecasts currently assume the Hammers will return to the top flight after just one season in the Championship.

Should West Ham remain outside the Premier League for another season, the estimated contractual loss provision would increase by a further £2.3m.

That is a sobering admission and demonstrates just how important Premier League football is to the stadium’s financial model.

London Stadium generated revenue of £13.6m during the year, including £4.8m received from West Ham for its use of the ground.

However, this is nowhere near enough to make the operation financially sustainable.

The accounts confirm that the stadium continues to rely on Greater London Authority funding, with a capital contribution of £21.876m received during the year.

The GLA has also provided a letter of support covering at least 12 months from approval of the accounts.

In other words, despite being home to a Premier League football club for almost a decade, the stadium remains dependent on public-sector financial backing.

There was also an interesting development in the long-running financial dispute between West Ham and London Stadium LLP.

The disagreement concerned a payment of approximately £3.6m, plus interest, connected with Daniel Křetínský’s investment in West Ham.

Following a legal battle and an appeal, London Stadium ultimately won the case, with the money released from escrow in April 2026.

The accounts reversed a £3.941m provision previously made for the dispute, helping improve the reported financial result.

There are clearly significant challenges ahead.

The stadium’s financial future depends on West Ham returning to the Premier League, attracting new commercial partnerships, maintaining GLA support and managing its expensive long-term contractual commitments.

The recent departure of chief executive Graham Gilmore after nine years in the role adds another layer of uncertainty, with operations director Darren Raczkowski stepping in as interim chief executive.

For West Ham supporters, there is an uncomfortable irony.

The club’s move to the London Stadium was supposed to provide a modern home and a platform for growth, while delivering a lasting legacy for London.

Yet almost a decade later, the stadium is still losing millions, carries an enormous long-term contractual burden and remains reliant on public money.

And with West Ham now in the Championship, the financial assumptions underpinning the stadium’s future are already under greater pressure.

The big question is how much longer London taxpayers will be expected to support an operation that has yet to demonstrate it can stand on its own two feet.

#1978. West Ham Boss Parker Makes January Admission On talkSPORT

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has made it clear that January transfers are not currently at the forefront of his thinking, despite the Hammers’ obvious need to strengthen their squad. Speaking to talkSPORT this morning, Parker suggested that his immediate priority is working with the players already at his disposal.

Asked directly whether West Ham would have money to spend and bring in fresh faces, Parker acknowledged that the January window would be considered if necessary. However, he explained that since arriving at Rush Green, his attention has been almost entirely focused on his players and coaching staff.

Personally, I think he’s absolutely right. Even with the best will in the world, and assuming West Ham bring in some brilliant players in January, there are still nearly two months’ worth of results to fight for with the players currently available. Parker would be absolutely mad to spend too much time concentrating on transfers now.

Speaking during his talkSPORT interview, Parker explained that he had barely spoken to anybody outside his immediate coaching environment since taking charge.

“I’m sure there’ll be an eye in January if need be,” he said, before explaining that his main priority was establishing the habits and principles he wants from his players.

West Ham have a director of football in Nils Koppen, who can deal with precisely this type of thing. There is no reason for Parker to be spending his first few weeks in the job obsessing about transfer targets when the current squad desperately needs coaching.

After all, Claret & Hugh has already revealed that Koppen is working on January recruitment, including an approach to a potential striker signing.

The work is happening behind the scenes, and Parker doesn’t need to be personally involved in every conversation.

Parker can outsource his transfer concerns to Koppen

As Claret & Hugh has already revealed following contact with the football club, January business is being planned.

Every message we’ve received from sources inside the club indicates that promotion back to the Premier League is the overwhelming priority.

Of course, I expect funds to be made available in January. That doesn’t mean West Ham have unlimited money to spend, but the club’s determination to get promoted has been made abundantly clear.

And whilst we’ve previously reported on the financial constraints surrounding January recruitment, that doesn’t mean the club will simply sit on its hands.

But the January transfer window cannot rescue the points we fail to collect in November and December.

That is why Parker is right to concentrate on coaching.

Another interesting aspect of the interview was Parker’s discussion of the mentality required to succeed in the Championship.

He explained that players coming down from the Premier League have often spent months losing football matches, only to find themselves suddenly expected to win almost every week.

That psychological transition, he suggested, can be enormous.

The players clearly have ability, but Parker needs to establish the mentality and habits that allow them to produce it consistently.

If he can do that over the next few weeks, West Ham will be in a considerably stronger position when January arrives.

And if Koppen can then strengthen the areas that need improving, all the better.

For now, though, I’m delighted Parker is concentrating on the job immediately in front of him.

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 12:00

Arsenal are reportedly making progress in contract negotiations for two more first-team stars after Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber.

#1976. West Ham Join Race For Serbian Teenager As January Priorities Emerge

West Ham United have reportedly joined Birmingham City and Southampton in monitoring Malmö FF midfielder Jovan Milosavljević, with the 19-year-old Serbian attracting attention ahead of the January transfer window. However, the latest transfer link raises a fairly obvious question about the Hammers’ recruitment priorities.

According to OnTheMinute, West Ham are keeping watch on the youngster, who joined Malmö from Serbian football earlier this year and is contracted to the Swedish club until December 2029. The report describes the interest as exploratory, rather than suggesting a bid is imminent.

And whilst I’m not going to get too upset about a transfer rumour, particularly one which makes it clear that West Ham are merely monitoring a player, I do wonder why we’re being linked with another midfielder. Probably the last thing West Ham need right now is another one, and certainly not somebody who may develop in time.

It’s important to note that Scott Parker’s squad already boasts five young midfielders in Divine Mukasa, Lewis Orford, Soungoutou Magassa, Arne Engels and Mohamadou Kanté.

That’s a considerable amount of talent, and whilst they’re all at different stages of their development, there are already questions about how Parker can accommodate them.

As Claret & Hugh previously pointed out, West Ham have something of an embarrassment of riches in midfield, with several players competing for relatively few positions.

And that’s before the likes of Tomáš Souček and Edson Álvarez are factored into the conversation.

I’m certainly not suggesting that Nils Koppen should stop scouting promising young footballers. That would be ridiculous, and identifying talent before it becomes expensive is clearly part of his job.

But there’s a difference between keeping an eye on a youngster and actually spending money on him.

Milosavljević may well develop into an excellent player, but West Ham already have several midfielders who need opportunities to develop themselves.

It would be clear to anyone who has seen the team play recently that goalkeeper, centre-back and striker are far more pressing concerns than an already bloated midfield.

We’ve seen the problems at the back, we’ve seen the difficulties in front of goal, and we’ve certainly seen enough to suggest that Scott Parker could do with some immediate reinforcements.

#1975. Premier League KMI Panel unanimously admits to another refereeing error which wronged Liverpool

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.

The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola said afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.

The Premier League’s KMI Panel has now published its findings from the most recent top-flight matchday (via premierleague.com), and all five independent assessors adjudged that the penalty award against Liverpool was incorrect.

However, there was also unanimous agreement that VAR was right not to intervene, as it was decreed that no ‘clear and obvious’ error had taken place.

The panel concluded: ‘The panel unanimously felt that the referee’s call of a penalty for a challenge by Kerkez on Osorio was incorrect, with the contact being inevitable given the jumping actions of both players.

‘However, the non-intervention of VAR was supported on the basis it was not a clear and obvious error.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Liverpool fans must be getting sick of hearing from the Premier League’s KMI Panel at this stage, with this incident coming fresh off the back of the panel ruling that we should’ve had a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the 0-1 defeat to Arsenal.

The incident with Kerkez and Osorio wasn’t as black-and-white, but the decision to award a spot kick still felt rather curious at the time. Luckily for Harrington, it came too late to have any major bearing on the overall result at Selhurst Park.

Still, to hear that an independent panel unanimously acknowledged that the Reds were wronged by another refereeing error is galling for everyone associated with LFC, and yet again it calls into question the standads of officiating in the Premier League.

It’s the kind of inconsistency between Kerkez having a spot kick given against him for a 50/50 duel, and Timber getting away with a blatant infringement, which drives players, coaches, fans and pundits absolutely berserk.

Thankfully the decision in the Palace game didn’t do any lasting harm for Liverpool, but you get the sense that it won’t be long before another contentious decision goes against us and the KPI Panel is wheeled out to tell us what we can already deduce for ourselves.

#1974. West Ham Exclusive: London Stadium Dispute Finally Resolved

Claret & Hugh understands that West Ham and the London Stadium have reached an agreement to host a West Ham Women’s WSL game at the London Stadium on a date yet to be scheduled.

Late last year, the two parties had a dispute over a West Ham WSL game being played at the London Stadium and looked set for another legal battle in the courts.

Under the 2013 concessionaire agreement, West Ham are allowed to play up to 25 competitive games at the London Stadium in return for an annual usage fee.

The index-linked usage fee has inflated from £2.5m in 2016 to £4.8m each year in 2025, meaning each of the 25 games cost West Ham around £192,000 per match last season.

West Ham wanted to use one of those 25 competitive games to play a West Ham Women’s WSL game, which is mandated by regulations, but the London Stadium owners refused to allow it at the time.

The breakthrough came during negotiations for West Ham’s backing for the 2029 World Athletics Championships, which London Stadium bid to host.

The bid required West Ham’s backing, which was secured in August this year, but ultimately the bid failed in September, having lost out to Nairobi.

Part of the concessions agreed in return for West Ham’s backing for the athletics championship bid included hosting a WSL game at the London Stadium.

#1972. Switzerland 4-0 Scotland: Andy Robertson sends stern warning to Sebastien Pocognoli after heavy loss ruins historic night

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 12:05

Scotland captain Andrew Robertson has insisted that new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli does not have time to turn their fortunes around after a heavy 4-0 defeat by Switzerland in the UEFA Nations League on Monday.

It was a bitter sweet night for Robertson at Berit Sitterstadion, as he won his 103rd international cap to become Scotland’s all-time record appearance-maker, surpassing Kenny Dalglish’s record that stood for 40 years.

However, Robertson’s personal achievement was soon overshadowed by a disappointing loss to Switzerland which has consigned them to a third-place finish in League B Group 1 of the Nations League.

Against a much-changed Swiss side, Scotland gifted the hosts a 22nd-minute lead when midfielder Lewis Ferguson inadvertently diverted a harmless cross into his own net.

Scotland’s alarming collapse in St Gallen began with two more goals conceded in the first six minutes of the second half, before Zeki Amdouni netted Switzerland’s fourth in the closing stages to rub salt into the visitors’ wounds.

"I thought first half we were in the game," Robertson told reporters after the match. "We lost a stupid goal but I thought we had chances and could easily have been one-each at half time.

"We talk about it at half time to say keep going and by 50 minutes we're 3-0 down. That cannot happen in international football.

"We were playing against a good team, but we were in the game in the first half. We have to do it for 90 minutes. Then you're 3-0 down at a tough place. A really tough night for us."

Scotland boss Pocognoli, who was appointed as Steve Clarke's successor in August, has previously called for patience as he attempts to implement an attacking philosophy with the national team.

However, the 39-year-old Belgian has prevailed in only two of his first six games in charge – both against North Macedonia – and the Tartan Army have seen their team concede 10 goals in the process.

Questioned on how long it might take for Pocognoli’s approach to yield positive results, Robertson warned: "I don't think you've got time in international football. You have to do it.

"Are those supporters who have travelled everywhere going to give us time? No. Are the people inside Hampden going to give us time? No.

“Are the people outside Hampden that are going to be critical, and rightly so, going to give us time? No. We've not got time. The players don't have time. We have to step up.

"We now have a long break until March which is not a good thing. It's going to be a tough one to swallow."

Having accumulated seven points from six Nations League games, Scotland have missed out on a quarter-final spot but have avoided relegation from League B.

Scotland will therefore have no competitive fixtures during the next international break in March 2027 when Pocognoli will instead prepare for friendly fixtures.

#1971. West Ham Linked With 6ft 4in Defender as Koppen Pledge is Put to The Test

West Ham United have reportedly joined the race for Stevenage defender Jack Taylor, with the 21-year-old currently impressing on loan at Exeter City. However, whilst the Hammers clearly need another centre-back, I’m struggling to understand why we’d be looking at another developing youngster.

According to Graeme Bailey at TEAMtalk, West Ham are among eight clubs monitoring the 6ft 4in defender, alongside Everton, Brighton, Brentford, Crystal Palace, Fulham, Millwall and Norwich. Taylor recently scored in Exeter’s FA Cup victory over Huddersfield, although there is no confirmation that West Ham had scouts at the match.

It’s clear as day that West Ham need a central defender amongst other positions, but quite why we’d be looking at a 21-year-old from Stevenage is anyone’s guess.

Airidas Golambeckis has represented England at youth level and looks to have incredible potential.

Indeed, his recent performances for England’s Under-20s have strengthened his case for a first-team opportunity, particularly with Max Kilman suspended against Preston.

I’ve been impressed by Golambeckis whenever I’ve seen him, and his performance against Stevenage earlier this year was one of the first occasions when his potential really caught my attention.

Signing Taylor would appear to go against Nils Koppen’s stated recruitment principle of not blocking the pathway of youngsters coming through the academy.

And I think this would definitely be one of those examples.

Airidas Golambeckis has earned the right to play for West Ham

Don’t get me wrong, I’m not averse to signing an experienced centre-back to see us over the line, in the same way that Axel Disasi came in during January last season.

West Ham’s lack of defensive depth is obvious, and we’ve previously highlighted the need for additional cover during a demanding Championship campaign.

But another young central defender to block the pathway of an exceptional talent at our own club?

And with Claret & Hugh having received confirmation from a club source that Konstantinos Mavropanos is not for sale in January, this shouldn’t be about finding his replacement.

If West Ham are going to strengthen at centre-back, I’d rather they signed somebody experienced enough to make an immediate difference to our promotion prospects.

Taylor might become an excellent defender, but we’ve already got a promising youngster who deserves his chance. Personally, I wouldn’t give this transfer rumour too much attention.

#1970. Vinicius Junior: Real Madrid star reveals impact of Arsenal transfer speculation with honest admission

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 12:10, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 12:10

Vinicius Junior has admitted that feeling “truly overwhelmed” by summer transfer speculation is partly to blame for his slow start to the season at Real Madrid.

The 26-year-old was allegedly targeted by Premier League champions Arsenal who were keen to explore a big-money move for the left-sided attacker as he approached the final 12 months of his contract.

However, a transfer to the Emirates Stadium failed to materialise and Vinicius opted to sign a new long-term contract at Real Madrid in August, keeping him at the Bernabeu until 2032.

Speculation over his future in the Spanish capital intensified shortly after Brazil's disappointing last-16 exit at the 2026 World Cup, which led to him not training as much as he should have by his own admission.

Under new Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho, Vinicius has been unable to reach the heights expected on a consistent basis, scoring just one goal and registering three assists in 12 appearances across all competitions this season.

Vinicius has since opened up on how a summer of speculation and an early World Cup exit has contributed to his drop-off in form at club level.

“I don’t think I prepared as well as I could have after the World Cup because the impact of that tournament is so significant for all Brazilians,” Vinicius said at a press conference in Singapore ahead of Brazil’s friendly on Tuesday.

“Being knocked out so early was something we hadn’t expected, so I took advantage of my holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family.

“I ended up training less than in previous years. That may have affected my start to the season.

“On ‌top of that, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs showing interest last summer, I felt truly overwhelmed, as with the situation at Real Madrid, but it’s a very long season.”

In October, Vinicius was handed a straight red card and a four-match suspension after pulling the hair of Villarreal midfielder Nathan Saliba.

Real Madrid’s club-record signing Yan Diomande has since flourished for Mourinho’s side in Vinicius’s preferred left-sided position, and the Brazilian has acknowledged that he has work to do to win back his place in the starting lineup.

“Maintaining such a high level for so long is always very difficult,” Real’s No.7 added.

“I think only Cristiano Ronaldo and [Lionel] Messi have managed to do this for so many years, reaching the same kinds of numbers. I am human, I often make mistakes, but I always try to improve.”

Since joining Real Madrid from Flamengo in 2018, Vinicius has played 387 times for the club across all competitions, recording 129 goals and 103 assists as well as winning three La Liga titles and two Champions Leagues.

Mourinho recently stated that he is confident that Vinicius will rediscover his top form with the Spanish giants in the not too distant future.

#1969. Ex-Premier League referee questions appointment of officials for Liverpool v Man United

A prominent former Premier League referee has questioned the selection of officiasl for the fixture between Liverpool and Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday.

As confirmed via premierleague.com, Sam Barrott will take charge of the match, with Adam Nunn and Lee Betts as his assistants, while Chris Kavanagh is fourth official. John Brooks is on VAR, assisted by Paul Howard.

The upcoming game is the Reds’ sixth home match in the top flight this season, and it’ll be the third to have had the Yorkshire native as the referee.

Upon learning that curious fact, Keith Hackett took to social media to endorse Barrott as a referee but question the decision-making process which has led to him being dispatched to Anfield once again.

The former chief executive of the PGMOL (now Pro Ref) posted on X: ‘A top-class referee, but not a very good appointing procedure by his bosses’.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

It’s a strong show of faith by Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb to assign Barrott to what is always the most high-profile fixture in English football, and arguably world football.

Liverpool fans might be forgiven for not being able to summon much enthusiasm over the appointment, given the official’s previous at Anfield this season.

In August, it was he who awarded Nottingham Forest a penalty in their 2-2 draw against the Reds when Neco Williams went to ground under a challenge from Alisson Becker. The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel subsequently adjudged that the spot kick was wrongly given.

While there are clear critera which must be observed when appointing match officials to specific fixtures – any officials from Merseyside or Manchester are obviously ineligible for Sunday’s clash at Anfield – seeing Barrott assigned to yet another Liverpool home game does seem anomalous.

We just hope – for his sake as much as anyone else’s – that the main talking point after the final whistle isn’t a controversial and decisive error on his part. The last thing we need is yet more dubious refereeeing affecting the Reds.

Stuttgart are supposedly unwilling to sanction a mid-season departure for the former Leicester playmaker, who is a regular starter for Sebastian Hoeness in the Bundesliga this term.

Adding to the difficulty of a potential deal, El Khannous recently signed a long-term contract with the German club, meaning that it would take a significant fee to prize him away from MHP Arena.

During his first campaign at MHP Arena, El Khannous helped Stuttgart to a fourth-placed finish in the Bundesliga, securing Champions League football for the current season.

Whilst Leeds are certainly a mid-ranking Premier League football, they are not currently in the position to offer European football, so a move to Elland Road would be a step down in that way.

However, the pull of the English game is strong, and there is a chance that El Khannous returns to the Premier League at some point, potentially during 2027's summer window.

#1960. ‘Did you see any problems?’ – Hungary boss defiant over Dominik Szoboszlai decision

Hungary manager Marco Rossi has defended his usage of Dominik Szoboszlai during this international window.

The Liverpool midfielder sprained his knee during the Reds’ 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace the weekend before last and admitted that he nearly pulled out of his country’s win over Georgia six days later.

His choice to represent his nation was condemned by some reporters back on Merseyside, amid fears of aggravating the injury and compromising his involvement for his club over the coming weeks as the fixtures come thick and fast for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Rossi was defiant when quizzed about Szoboszlai ahead of Hungary’s match against Northern Ireland on Tuesday night.

He told reporters (via Origo Sport): “Did you see any problems with Dominik in the Georgia game? Because I didn’t see any. He played like he usually does, so there are no problems from our side. He says he’s ready, he’s available, so he’ll play.”

The Hungary boss was true to his word, as the Liverpool star played the entirety of the Northern Ireland game, thankfully seeming to come through it without any adverse effects.

#1957. Tottenham given Harry Kane transfer hope despite Bayern Munich contract renewal (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 17 Nov 2026 16:41, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 16:41

Harry Kane could be tempted by a move back to Tottenham Hotspur if he wins the Champions League with Bayern Munich, but under certain conditions, a former Spurs striker has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Kane is gearing up for a return to domestic football after breaking the England all-time men's appearance record during the November international break, in addition to scoring in back-to-back games against Croatia and Spain.

The 33-year-old also made headlines off the field recently by signing a new contract with Bayern to the summer of 2029, and he already boasts 20 goal involvements in 15 games for the Bavarians this season; 10 of his own and 10 assists.

However, speculation surrounding a possible return to Tottenham one day continues to linger, as the Lilywhites reportedly retain the right to match any bid that comes in from another club for their all-time top scorer.

Sports Mole recently asked Darren Bent about Tottenham's chances of re-signing Kane, and the ex-Spurs striker can see the England captain being tempted to go back to England, but only if the Lilywhites are competing in the top half of the table.

"We saw that new contract, which they were delighted about. The way Kane spoke, there was no real urgency to get back to the Premier League, but you never know," Bent said via MrQ betting site.

"If Bayern win the Champions League this year, then I guess he's ticked every box he wants to tick. He's won the league over there, and he's won trophies over there.

"He's won the Golden Boot. The big one would be the Champions League. If he could go over there and win that, it puts him in a different bracket, certainly over there, because you look at the great strikers Bayern Munich have had, they've all won the Champions League. Lewandowski, these types of players.

"I'm guessing that's the last box he's got to tick. If Kane was to go and win the Champions League this year, there's no reason why he couldn't then go, 'There's nothing more for me to achieve over there if I've won all the big trophies there are to win in Germany. Let me come back and see where Spurs are and potentially get a move there.'

"But then again, it all depends on where Spurs are, because there's no point in leaving Bayern Munich if Spurs are languishing at the bottom of the table, fighting relegation, or even in the bottom half of the table. What's he coming back for?"

When Kane departed Tottenham for Bayern Munich in the summer of 2023, he left with the second-highest goals total in the history of the Premier League, racking up 213 English top-flight strikes.

However, the striker left before he could either match or surpass Alan Shearer's unrivalled total of 260 Premier League goals; he needs another 47 to draw level with the Newcastle United legend.

During Kane's final year at Tottenham, Shearer expressed complete confidence that the Ballon d'Or winner would break his record one day, having been told of Kane's desire to do so by the man himself.

"I know how much he wants it - he's told me - which is fine, because I was exactly the same," Shearer said in an interview with the Premier League.

However, Kane then told FourFourTwo in September that the desire had 'diminished', so if he is to head back to his homeland, finally winning a trophy with Tottenham is likely to be his primary motivator.

Darren Bent was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of MrQ Live Casino.

#1955. New manager bounce? How Mauricio Pochettino fared in his first match in charge of previous clubs

Liverpool will be wary of the threat of ‘new manager bounce’ on Sunday when they face a Manchester United team now under the management of Mauricio Pochettino.

Having sacked Michael Carrick last Thursday, the Red Devils moved swiftly to appoint the Argentine as his successor, with their new head coach signing off from a similar role with the United States with a 2-0 win over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League.

The Old Trafford outfit enjoyed an immediate upsurge in form when their former midfielder replaced Ruben Amorim back in January, but how has the new man in charge fared in his first game at his five previous spells as a club boss?

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Espanyol were in the LaLiga relegation zone when Pochettino took charge almost 18 years ago, and his first task seemed a daunting one against city rivals Barcelona, who’d end the season as treble winners under Pep Guardiola.

The Argentine had only two training sessions to implement his methods before the Copa Del Rey derby fixture, but his new team claimed an impressive share of the spoils on home turf before narrowly losing the second leg 3-2 at Camp Nou. A few weeks later, he masterminded a shock league victory at the home of their arch-rivals.

The Saints’ decision to axe the popular Nigel Adkins mid-season was met with shock throughout English football, with the south coast club well on their way to staying up in their first season back in the Premier League after a seven-year absence.

He again drew 0-0 in his first game of a managerial spell, with Southampton putting in a battling performance against an Everton side who, at the time, were outside contenders for Champions League qualification under David Moyes.

This was Pochettino’s first time having a full summer to prepare for a managerial job rather than coming in mid-season, earning the Spurs gig off the back of his fine work at Southampton.

The north Londoners survived a red card and a missed Mark Noble penalty before snatching all three points in stoppage time courtesy of an Eric Dier goal on what was also his first outing with Tottenham, who left the Boleyn Ground with a sweet win over their capital rivals.

It was back to mid-season appointments for Pochettino six-and-a-half years later as he filled the vacancy left by Thomas Tuchel’s departure for Chelsea.

He maintained his record of never losing his first game in charge of a club, but in truth this was two points dropped for PSG, who at the time were three points adrift of surprise Ligue 1 leaders Lyon. They also had to come from behind against an in-form Les Verts side.

Sunday won’t be the first time that Liverpool provide the opposition for Pochettino in his first game in charge – the Reds also had that role when the Argentine began his reign as Chelsea boss three years ago.

Once again he’d end with a draw, as an entertaining clash on the opening weekend of the Premier League season saw Luis Diaz’s opener for the visitors cancelled out by Axel Disasi as each team had a further goal disallowed.

Four draws and a win for Pochettino from his managerial debuts at his previous clubs – it’s a respectable record, but not an overly intimidating one.

It feels more pertinent to look at his first results when taking charge mid-season, just as he’s doing now with Man United. All three of those games were drawn, and another such result on Sunday would be regarded as a decent start for him.

It’d also represent disappointment for Liverpool, who are without an Anfield win over their arch-rivals in three attempts since the famous 7-0 romp in March 2023.

#1952. Cruzeiro vs Palmeiras - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 17 Nov 2026 17:17, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 09:25

Cruzeiro will be looking to strengthen their hopes of securing a direct place in the Copa Libertadores when they welcome Palmeiras to Mineirao on Wednesday in the Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A.

The hosts have enjoyed a remarkable turnaround under Artur Jorge, climbing from the bottom of the table to third place with 60 points after winning their last four league matches, while the visitors remain firmly in the title race, sitting second with 73 points, three behind leaders Flamengo.

Cruzeiro's transformation under Jorge has been one of the most impressive stories of the Brazilian top-flight campaign, with the Portuguese coach overseeing a dramatic recovery after taking charge of a team that had collected just four points from their opening eight matches.

From the ninth round through to the 34th, the Foxes accumulated 56 points, a tally bettered only by Flamengo during that period and even superior to Palmeiras' return over the same stretch.

Their improvement has been particularly evident in recent weeks, with four consecutive victories providing further evidence of a side that has developed greater consistency and resilience when faced with difficult situations.

Cruzeiro demonstrated those qualities in their most recent outing against Bahia, recovering from an early setback to secure a comeback 3-2 victory.

Kaio Jorge was instrumental in the turnaround, scoring twice, while Bruno Rodrigues also found the net to complete an impressive result that strengthened their position in the top three.

With their qualification for next season's Copa Libertadores already secured, Cruzeiro's immediate objective is to guarantee direct entry into the competition, making Wednesday's encounter particularly important with two consecutive away fixtures to follow.

Indeed, Palmeiras arrive with an impressive away record, having collected 31 points from 17 matches on their travels, suffering just two defeats in the process.

The visitors also boast the league's strongest defensive record, having conceded only 23 goals, while their current 11-match unbeaten run in the Brasileirao underlines their consistency during the closing stages of the campaign.

Abel Ferreira's side were particularly ruthless in their previous league outing, producing a dominant first-half display to establish a 4-0 advantage before eventually recording a 6-1 victory over Remo.

Nevertheless, the visitors' demanding schedule could become a significant factor on Wednesday, having recently booked their place in the Copa do Brasil final despite losing 2-1 to Vasco da Gama in the second leg of their semi-final before progressing on penalties.

With Palmeiras still competing on three fronts, Ferreira must carefully manage his available resources, particularly with several players having only recently returned from international duty.

The title race also leaves little room for error, as Palmeiras cannot afford to drop points if they are to maintain pressure on Flamengo before the two sides meet on November 21.

Even a victory at Mineirao would leave the second-placed side dependent on Flamengo dropping points elsewhere, but that possibility could encourage the visitors to adopt a more adventurous approach as the contest develops.

Cruzeiro will make several changes to the side that defeated Bahia, with Jonathan Jesus and Kaua Moraes unavailable through suspension, while Wesley is also ruled out following a decision by the Superior Court of Sports Justice (STJD).

Bruno Rodrigues will miss the encounter because of contractual restrictions, while Keny Arroyo is unlikely to feature after representing Ecuador during the international break.

There is better news for Artur Jorge, however, as William, Lucas Villalba and Matheus Pereira are available again following their respective suspensions, while Fabricio Bruno has returned to training with the squad and could provide an important defensive boost.

Joao Marcelo, Gabriel Pec and Luis Sinisterra remain in recovery, with Felipe Morais, Kaique Kenji and Ze Lucas still needing further assessments before their availability can be determined.

Palmeiras also have several selection concerns following the international break, with Gustavo Gomez and Mauricio unlikely to return in time for Wednesday's contest.

Agustin Giay, Flaco Lopez and Jhon Arias travelled to Brazil on chartered flights during the early hours of Wednesday and are expected to join the squad directly in Belo Horizonte, although their involvement from the start remains uncertain.

Defensively, Ferreira will be without Joaquin Piquerez, who sustained an injury while representing Uruguay, and Murilo, who continues his recovery from a left thigh problem.

Bruno Fuchs and Alexander Barboza are therefore expected to form the central defensive partnership, with Khellven and Artur providing the options in the full-back positions, although Emiliano Martinez could drop into defence if Ferreira opts for a three-man backline.

Marlon Freitas, Lucas Evangelista and Andreas Pereira are among the midfielders expected to provide the necessary balance, while Ramon Sosa, Vitor Roque and Felipe Anderson are competing for attacking positions.

Flaco Lopez and Jhon Arias could initially be named among the substitutes as Palmeiras look to manage their workload following their late return from international duty.

Otavio; William, Bruno, Villalba, Vina; Romero, Henrique; Gerson, Pereira, Marquinhos; Jorge

Miguel; Khellven, Fuchs, Barboza, Artur; Freitas, Evangelista, Pereira, Anderson; Sosa, Roque

The visitors' demanding schedule and selection problems could prevent them from operating at their usual level, but their ability to exploit spaces in transition should still create opportunities against an ambitious Cruzeiro side.

We expect a closely-contested encounter, with neither team doing quite enough to establish control over the other, and a share of the spoils appears to be the most likely outcome.

#1940. Liverpool must make January signing after telling Trey Nyoni comments

Trey Nyoni has admitted he ‘enjoys’ playing in the six position, but that it’s still a ‘new position’ for him.

The young Englishman has caught the eye with his performances at L4 this term, earning three straight starts across clashes with Arsenal (Premier League), Chelsea (Carabao Cup) and Fenerbahce (Champions League).

However, the teenager’s admission ultimately raises concerns around the midfield department ahead of the January transfer window.

It’s reassuring that links to Lamine Camara (who came close to a switch to Chelsea in the summer) have resurfaced ahead of the winter, given ongoing concerns over how Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch fit in an Andoni Iraola side.

While the performances of Alexis Mac Allister and Nyoni have undoubtedly mitigated matters, the truth of the matter is that Liverpool can’t look to rely on the latter of the duo throughout an entire campaign.

The Reds must, and no doubt will, look after the teenager to ensure his excellent development carries on smoothly, but his recent comments are a clear reminder that investment midway through the campaign is a necessity.

“I’ve been playing like a number six. I played there when I was young but, to be honest, it’s a new position for me. I’ve had to learn a lot in a short space of time,” Nyoni told The Inside Scoop (via BBC Sport).

“I enjoy playing like a six because I can get on the ball and always try to play forwards, but I enjoy playing as an eight as well.

“I like to drop in, get the ball and play forward but I’ve had to learn the discipline of being a number six.

“Right now, I don’t really have a preference. As I’m starting out, I enjoy playing both.”

We have faith that Iraola’s demands will eventually click with Gravenberch and Szoboszlai, but it’s still painful to see how open Liverpool look in the middle of the park when Mac Allister is forced to share space with either of his senior midfield partners. And the less said about a double pivot consisting of the Dutchman and the Hungarian, the better.

Yes, it’s fair to point out that our season is far from spiralling under Iraola — the Reds sit fourth in the Premier League table with only four points standing between them and Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Brighton in second.

But it does feel like there is an opportunity for Liverpool to make a modest statement in 2026/27. Not quite title glory, it has to be said, but certainly to stake a claim as “best of the rest” and set a promising foundation for the seasons to come under Iraola.

Adding an additional midfielder (like, cough cough, Lamine Camara, cough cough) to the ranks who can carry out the Basque’s demands would undoubtedly serve that purpose.

Elsewhere, the backline looks in fine shape and the forward line evidently needs time to gel. Give the manager the tools he needs in midfield and this could be an impressive opening campaign for Andoni Iraola.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Now, though, everyone would be glad that the decision was made to sign the young Italian. To say he’s exploded this season would be an understatement and he’s perhaps the biggest gem at the club right now.

“We had a scout who worked near Verona and he immediately pointed out this boy to us, Alphadjo Cisse, who played for the Under-17s and then for the Primavera, and then for the Under-20s. So we went to see him and he was very interesting.

“Two or three years ago, we launched Milan Futuro. Our idea was to sign him for that team a year earlier, but we couldn’t reach an agreement with Hellas Verona. They wanted to keep him and decided to send him on loan to Serie B.

“We followed him very closely in Serie B, too, and he literally exploded there in the first six months. We told ourselves he’d made such a good transition from the Primavera and Verona’s bench to Serie B that we needed to make a move.

“It was winter and we had to hurry. If he had gone to PSV and you had wanted to buy him later, perhaps after playing in the Champions League, the price would have risen to €30 or €40 million. Sometimes you have to speed things up a bit.”

Considering the club had followed him since he was in the Under-17s, it’s a good thing they eventually managed to sign him, especially with the way he’s started at San Siro.

#1924. Rayan to Liverpool or Manchester United? How the Brazilian’s style suits both clubs

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 18:16

Rayan is living a fast-moving career in European football. Signed by Bournemouth in January 2026 after standing out at Vasco da Gama, the Brazilian forward quickly won a place in the Premier League and began attracting the attention of bigger clubs. Liverpool are already monitoring his progress, while a statement has put Manchester United in the conversation: the player revealed that he has always supported the Red Devils because of Cristiano Ronaldo.

Andoni Iraola, who worked with Rayan at Bournemouth, took charge of Liverpool at the start of 2026-27. Manchester United have just appointed Mauricio Pochettino, a manager known for developing young attackers and for implementing a high-intensity style. But which of the two clubs would be the better destination for the Brazilian? The answer depends less on Rayan’s personal preference and more on the characteristics that have made him one of the most interesting prospects in Brazilian football.

Bournemouth paid Vasco €35m (about £30m) in January 2026, betting on a 19-year-old forward. Adaptation was quick: Rayan scored five goals and provided two assists in 15 games in the second half of last season.

His profile is different from a traditional winger who relies on short dribbles and quick changes of direction to beat a marker. Rayan is a player of strength and acceleration. When he receives with space, he can carry the ball at speed, protect possession with his body and attack the box with few touches.

In the 2025 Brazilian Serie A, Rayan was the player who finished the most carries with a shot, with 33 occasions. He also scored 14 goals in the league, a number that placed him among the competition’s top scorers. The forward is not just a winger who cuts inside, however. Under Fernando Diniz at Vasco, he was also used centrally, as a centre-forward, and showed an ability to win aerial balls and shield possession with his back to goal. His height and physical strength make it possible to imagine growth in that role, although he still has to improve his control and combination play under pressure.

It is also important to consider what is left to develop. Rayan can still improve the quality of his final pass, his choice of moments to shoot and his involvement in building play. Despite the volume of carries that ended in shots, his creative output was more limited. That helps explain why he still needs an environment that gives him freedom to attack without requiring him to be the main organiser of the attack.

This season, the Brazilian has played ten Premier League games, with one goal and no assists. The output does not match his arrival in England, but Rayan remains a frequent starter and is still adapting to a new manager and a model different from Iraola’s.

Liverpool’s interest strengthened after Iraola’s arrival. The Reds followed the Brazilian closely early in the season and could consider a move in 2027. Iraola knows Rayan’s virtues and limitations. It was under his management that the Brazilian began adapting to the intensity of the Premier League, playing mainly on the right and being given freedom to attack space.

The manager also played a part in the step up of other Bournemouth players, such as Antoine Semenyo, who stood out before moving to Manchester City. Tactically, the combination makes sense. Iraola’s teams usually press high, try to win the ball back in advanced areas and accelerate as soon as they find space. He does not demand that his wingers stay tied to the touchline: they can attack inside, combine with the full-backs and appear in different channels. Rayan could play on the right, cutting inside onto his left foot, but also attack depth and offer a physical threat in transitions.

At Liverpool, that characteristic could be useful. The team has changed in attack: Bradley Barcola, Cody Gakpo, Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha offer alternatives, but Rayan would add a different profile, a more powerful forward able to carry the ball at speed and attack the box.

There is one caveat. Liverpool already have quality attacking options. The manager also has to manage a more demanding calendar and a team with title ambitions. Rayan could find a way to play, but would hardly have the same freedom as a young player developing at Bournemouth.

Rayan’s link with Manchester United came to light in an interview with ESPN. The forward said he has always supported the club in England because of Cristiano Ronaldo, his great idol. He also recalled the emotion of playing at Old Trafford and beating the Red Devils 3-0 with Bournemouth in October.

The statement became relevant when United hired Pochettino to try to reorganise a team going through a difficult season. The Argentinian has a track record of developing young players and built his best work in England with intense teams, aggressive in the press and quick in transitions. His most usual model starts from a 4-2-3-1, with wingers who often attack inside spaces and full-backs who push on to give width.

That structure could favour Rayan. Starting from the right, the Brazilian would have freedom to carry towards the box, finish with his left foot and attack the spaces created by team-mates’ movement. High pressing also suits his physical ability, although defensive involvement is still an area he needs to improve.

The problem is competition. United already have Bryan Mbeumo, Amad Diallo and Matheus Cunha among their attacking options, plus Benjamin Sesko as a central reference. There is also a developmental question. Pochettino usually demands a lot from his players without the ball and works with coordinated attacking movements. For a forward who still needs to improve decision-making and creation, the environment can be positive but also brings high demands. The Brazilian would need to learn to alternate individual carrying with quick combination play and movement without the ball.

United, on the other hand, could offer room to grow if Pochettino sees Rayan as a medium-term project and not an immediate solution to attacking problems. The Argentinian’s ability to develop young forwards is a point in favour, but the squad already has players in similar roles.

Between the two scenarios, Liverpool appear to offer the clearer fit. Iraola already knows the Brazilian, knows how to use his strength in transitions and has a model that favours attackers able to carry the ball at speed. The departure of Mohamed Salah has also opened space for a reorganisation of the right side, making the position a concrete possibility for Rayan.

Manchester United have the emotional appeal and a manager whose philosophy could match the Brazilian’s characteristics. But the presence of Mbeumo, Amad and Cunha makes the battle for space more complex. To turn admiration for the club into a transfer, Rayan would need to see a clear sporting plan.

At any rate, the moment is still one of development. At 20, the forward does not need to choose immediately between two giants, especially as he has a contract with Bournemouth until 2031 and is still gaining experience in a demanding league. Rayan has the attributes to reach a top-level club, but his next step needs to be defined by the project that best uses his potential. Between his familiarity with Iraola and his identification with United, Liverpool appear to have a tactical advantage.

#1922. Sergio Navarro’s style and the key individuals: Milan Futuro tactical analysis

Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

With promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

Milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

This also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

Similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

Milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

Milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most important aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

Rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

Perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

At times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

Former Airdrieonians midfielder Justin Devenny was the hero for Northern Ireland as his wonder strike in the 1-1 draw with Hungary sealed their shock promotion to League A of the Nations League at the Puskas Arena.

Managed on the touchline by former Rangers hero Steven Davis in Budapest, the 41-year-old stepped into the head coach role on a crucial night for Northern Ireland, with manager Michael O’Neill suspended and forced to watch from the stands.

Promoted to League B during their last Nations League campaign, Northern Ireland entered Tuesday night’s game in remarkable form. Top of the group ahead of kick-off, they’d won three and drawn two, without conceding a single goal.

Requiring just a draw against Hungary to seal back-to-back Nations League promotion, they came under heavy pressure in the opening stages, with the home side finally breaking Northern Ireland’s resistance in the 35th minute when Barnabas Varga capitalised on a mistake from Trai Hume to place beyond Pierce Charles as the visitors conceded for the first time in 500 minutes.

Northern Ireland players vigorously appealed for a penalty after Ciaron Brown went down under a challenge from Andras Schafer in the area in the build-up to the goal, with Hungary’s subsequent clearance directly leading to Varga’s opener. However, referee Marco Guida waved away protests following a VAR check.

Searching for the goal that would secure a first promotion to League A, Northern Ireland battled back after the restart and thought they’d levelled when Isaac Price cannoned a long-range effort off the post just after the hour mark.

They found their equaliser shortly afterwards, though, and it was definitely worth the wait. A long throw from Sunderland defender Hume was half-cleared by the Hungarian defence before falling to Devenny, who took a deft first touch to control the ball, before flicking it up and blasting a volley into the top corner.

Despite being born in Irvine, the 23-year-old is eligible to play for Northern Ireland due to his grandparents. Devenny told the Belfast Telegraph that he opted to represent Northern Ireland after they approached him first and showed genuine faith in his abilities before Scotland did. During the interview, he emphasized that he chose to play for the nation he felt actively wanted him.

He began his career in the Kilmarnock youth system and spent time on loan with Broomhill and Airdrieonians before signing for the Diamonds on a permanent deal in the summer of 2022. His impressive form in the Scottish Championship won him a shock move to the English Premier League with Crystal Palace just 12 months later.

Playing over 50 games for the Eagles, the versatile midfielder won the Conference League, the FA Cup and the Community Shield during his time at Selhurst Park, before moving to EFL Championship side Stoke City for an undisclosed fee on deadline day. Scoring a brace on his debut for the club in a 4–0 win over Charlton Athletic, he’s been a regular for the Potters as they chase promotion to the top flight.

#1920. Declan Rice’s new five-year deal to 2031 marks his rise from £105m signing to Arsenal leader

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 18:28

Declan Rice’s new contract with Arsenal recognises a transformation built over three seasons. When he arrived at the Emirates Stadium in July 2023, the midfielder was a high-impact signing: he cost £105m, a record for a British player at the time, and carried the expectation of lifting a team that had just lost the Premier League title to Manchester City.

Today, at 27, Rice is an English champion, one of the leaders of the dressing room and one of the team’s technical reference points. The new five-year deal shows Arsenal’s intention to keep him at the centre of the project through his physical and technical peak. It also reflects his changing status within the club, as Rice is expected to earn a salary close to that of Bukayo Saka, until now the squad’s top earner.

Rice was not just an expensive signing who lived up to expectations. He became a more complete player, widened his influence across different phases of play and took on responsibilities beyond his role in midfield. The promise of 2023 has become one of the faces of a championship team and a leader for the cycle that starts now.

Rice’s arrival came at a decisive moment for Mikel Arteta’s project. In 2022-23, Arsenal spent much of the season at the top but lost steam in the closing stretch and finished five points behind Manchester City. The team had shown that they could compete for the title, but they needed more quality, depth and experience to sustain a challenge to the end.

Rice had characteristics that answered several of those needs. At 24, he was already West Ham United’s captain, had experience with England and had just won the Conference League. Arsenal beat the competition and completed the signing for £100m fixed plus £5m in bonuses.

The fee raised expectations. It was not enough for Rice to be a good holding midfielder: he had to justify a historic investment and help Arsenal take the step needed to compete with City. His first season showed the scale of the signing quickly.

Rice played 38 Premier League games, scoring seven goals and providing eight assists. The number of goal contributions was a considerable improvement on his West Ham record, but his impact was not limited to attacking output. Arsenal again finished as runners-up, but Rice had already become one of the team’s most important players. The signing did not deliver an immediate title, but it helped turn expectation into a conviction that the club had found a midfielder able to carry their project for many years.

Rice’s development also reflects the way Arteta changed his use. Early in his time at Arsenal, the Englishman often played as the deepest midfielder, responsible for protecting the defence and offering a reference point for build-up. It was a familiar role, close to the one he had at West Ham, but it did not use his full repertoire.

After an adaptation period, especially from the start of 2024, Arteta began using him more often as a box-to-box midfielder on the left. The change let Rice use one of his main qualities: carrying the ball at speed, breaking lines and arriving in the opposition area while still contributing to defensive recovery.

The Englishman gained more freedom to attack space, appear at the edge of the box and join attacking combinations. His physical power became a weapon for taking Arsenal into the opposition half, while his ability to get back helped keep balance when the team lost the ball. Instead of just protecting team-mates, Rice also began to drive the team.

Set pieces were another important tool. Rice began taking corners and free-kicks, using the accuracy of his delivery and his ability to put the ball in dangerous areas. Since his arrival, he has provided ten assists from set pieces in the Premier League. His two free-kick goals against Real Madrid in the 2024-25 Champions League quarter-finals were the most emblematic moment of that evolution.

Versatility does not mean Rice has no fixed position or needs to take part in every attacking action. The most recent development lies in choosing moments. With Martin Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Odegaard offering different partnership options, Arteta has alternated the height at which the Englishman receives the ball and the freedom he has to advance.

The ability to perform different roles is one of the reasons Rice has become so important to Arteta. In the title-winning season, he was used both as the most advanced midfielder and in a midfield pair alongside Zubimendi. He is not just a player who adapts to different positions: he lets the manager change the structure of the team without necessarily changing personnel.

Rice’s growth was not only tactical. Over the seasons, he also became one of the squad’s main voices. His direct personality, willingness to demand more from team-mates and ability to take responsibility in difficult moments made him a reference point for the group.

One example came in April, when Odegaard was out injured and Rice was given the captain’s armband. He had worn it on other occasions, but the choice reinforced a perception that had been building: his influence does not depend on being the official captain.

In Arsenal’s 2025-26 Premier League title, which ended a 22-year wait for the competition, Rice was one of the protagonists of the campaign, with 36 appearances, four goals and five assists in the league. More than his statistical contribution, his ability to maintain intensity in different roles was fundamental.

Declan Rice at Arsenal - all competitions since joining in July 2023 2023-24: 51 games, 48 starts, 33 wins, 8 draws, 10 defeats, 7 goals, 9 assists (64.7% wins) 2024-25: 52 games, 48 starts, 28 wins, 16 draws, 8 defeats, 9 goals, 10 assists (53.8% wins) 2025-26: 55 games, 49 starts, 37 wins, 12 draws, 6 defeats, 5 goals, 9 assists (67.3% wins) 2026-27 (in progress): 15 games, 14 starts, 13 wins, 1 draw, 1 defeat, 1 goal, 5 assists (86.7% wins) Total: 173 games, 159 starts, 111 wins, 37 draws, 25 defeats, 22 goals, 33 assists (64.2% wins)

The challenge now is to sustain this level without ignoring fatigue. Rice has come from seasons with a high volume of games, often exceeding 50 matches for club and country. Last season, he played 54 games for Arsenal in all competitions, in addition to England commitments. Managing his workload will be important for him to keep his influence over a demanding calendar.

By extending his contract to 2031, Arsenal secure a player who still has years at his peak ahead and who already knows Arteta’s demands in depth. The club no longer need to wait for Rice to become a leader: that stage has already happened. Now the expectation is that he helps lead the next chapters of a project that intends to keep competing for the main trophies.

Celtic’s board have been slammed for their lack of ambition and told it feels like they have “no plan” for when Martin O’Neill finally exits his role as manager.

Main shareholder Dermot Desmond and the board have faced several protests over the last 12 months, with the hierarchy at loggerheads with Celtic support over how the club is run, their perceived lack of footballing ambition and player recruitment.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recently, ultras fan group The Green Brigade has announced a boycott of all Scottish Cup matches and home Europa League fixtures, and former Celtic winger Charlie Nicholas admits he is concerned for the Scottish champions’ future, with tensions building ahead of the club’s annual AGM next month.

“Dermot Desmond is doing everything he can to frustrate the hardcore fans by not spending any money,” said Nicholas, speaking on the No Tippy Tappy Football Podcast from Footy Accumulators and BOYLE Sports. “They’re in turmoil with supporters, and that’s not going to go away. There’s an AGM coming up on 1 December, which was chaotic last season. They had to abandon it, and I don’t know how they’re going to get around this.

“There’s talk it might go digital rather than in person. But they’ve got major overheads, and Martin and his staff are finding it difficult to overcome this, because a lot of supporters aren’t going. Our judgement of Celtic is always going to be about Europe. We’ve won one game, and we only just got through it at the tail end of the other week. It’s not been good. The standard at the moment is very disappointing, to say the least.”

Nicholas, who won every domestic honour with Celtic during two spells in his playing career, is also concerned about how the club will replace veteran manager O’Neill when he decides his time in the game is over. The 74-year-old signed a one-year contract with the option of a further year in the summer. However, Nicholas isn’t convinced the club has a plan in place for when the Irishman boss calls time on his management.

Former Celtic loanee Robbie Keane was strongly linked to the vacant role in the summer, but talks were shelved after backlash from fans who were angered by the 46-year-old’s decision to remain in charge of Israeli side Maccabi Tel Aviv during the outbreak of the nation’s war against Gaza in 2023, with a section of Celtic fans openly supporting Palestine in the conflict.

“There have been a few suggested replacements for Martin O’Neill,” said Nicholas. “The strong talk in the summer was that they went after Robbie Keane. The word was that he more or less had the job, and that he’s still sitting in the background. That leads me into the debate that will continue with some sections of the Celtic fans and the shareholders. Until they get round that, there doesn’t look to be any evidence of a plan.

“What’s the next step of the ladder? Are we ready for Martin when he leaves? No, I don’t think they are ready. I just don’t know if the major shareholder is really wholehearted about it. There’s no one at the football club taking that responsibility now, so we’re drifting along at the moment. That’s why I understand where the real Celtic fans’ frustration is.”

#1917. Flamengo vs Athletico Paranaense - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 17 Nov 2026 19:11

With four rounds remaining in the Brasileirao, Flamengo host Athletico Paranaense on Wednesday night, November 18, as their title defence enters its decisive stage.

Having collected 92% of the available points in the second half of the season, Flamengo can take a significant step towards back-to-back titles and put themselves in a stronger position ahead of their huge clash against Palmeiras in the following round. Athletico Paranaense, meanwhile, face an uphill task to break back into the top four, having gone four matches without a win and with the tournament's leading scorer unavailable.

In the fight for back-to-back titles and a ninth Brasileirao crown, Flamengo return from this FIFA international break with good news: their key players delivered excellent performances and, more importantly, came back from international duty without any injuries.

Giorgian de Arrascaeta once again took centre stage for the Rubro-Negro with the Uruguay national team. Having had a direct hand in both of Uruguay’s goals against Argentina at the Bombonera, Flamengo’s number 10 also became the first foreigner to have a bust unveiled at the club’s headquarters, in a ceremony on Sunday, November 15.

Bruno Henrique also received the honour and looked ahead to the business end of the season: “We know there is not much left before the year ends, there are four games, so we will give everything in these games to win the title. God willing, we can celebrate in December as well,” he said at the event.

Right-back Guillermo Varela, meanwhile, produced a solid display, playing the full 95 minutes of the match in Buenos Aires. Although Argentina’s goal came down his side, he was not at fault.

Nicolas de la Cruz and Ecuadorians Gonzalo Plata and Anthony Valencia did not leave the bench, but the latter two still have a friendly against Bolivia on Tuesday night, November 17.

Athletico Paranaense, for their part, are enjoying a notable campaign for a newly promoted side. However, in the fight for a direct spot in next season’s Libertadores, the Furacao suffered a heavy blow at Brazil’s sports court (STJD).

In a hearing on Monday, November 16, Kevin Viveros had his ban extended to three matches. The Brasileirão’s top scorer with 21 goals was sent off in the 3-1 defeat to Vasco on November 4, for a stamp on full-back Cuiabano.

As a result, he will not return until the final round, against Sao Paulo at the Arena da Baixada. Jorge Rivaldo and Renan Peixoto are the natural options given their profile, but manager Odair Hellmann could also opt to use forward Kerwin Vargas in an adapted role.

In the same hearing, the Parana side were also punished. The fine for racist gestures attributed to a fan during the match against Vasco was increased to R$30,000 (approximately £4,200). The decision was taken by a majority of votes.

Currently fifth with 54 points, Athletico could close the gap on Fluminense, who occupy the final Libertadores spot. Bahia and Atletico Mineiro, however, are also in the same points range.

In a late development, Gonzalo Plata was released from the Ecuador squad for “personal reasons” and could become an unexpected boost. Having played just 13 minutes against Costa Rica, he should not, in theory, show any physical wear.

Nicolas de la Cruz and Anthony Valencia remain with their national teams and are not expected to return in time.

On the medical front, experienced left-back Alex Sandro has recovered from muscular oedema in his left thigh and has returned to training with the group, although Ayrton Lucas is expected to be the first choice for Portuguese manager Leonardo Jardim.

Midfielder Lucas Paqueta has not yet fully recovered from a knee problem sustained during the thrashing of Vasco, so he is unlikely to be included without a reasonable amount of training, according to Jardim himself. Danilo, meanwhile, continues his recovery schedule following a jaw fracture and also remains sidelined.

The point of concern is the number of players one booking away from suspension: Leo Pereira, Alex Sandro, Erick Pulgar, Arrascaeta, Pedro, Bruno Henrique, Luiz Araujo and Vitao. Should any of them be booked by referee Rafael Klein, they would miss the clash against Palmeiras in the following round.

Besides Viveros, Dantas is also serving a suspension due to the automatic one-match ban for a third yellow card. Young centre-back Arthur Dias, who is attracting interest from several European clubs, is another absentee. He is set to play for the Brazil national team against Singapore and is not expected to return to Brazil in time.

Defender Lucas Esquivel is still recovering from a hip injury and will be assessed on matchday, but he is expected to complete the back line alongside Gaston Benavidez and Juan Aguirre. Goalkeeper Santos and Bruno Zapelli could be given a chance in the starting eleven.

Agustin Rossi; Varela, Leo Pereira, Leo Ortiz, Ayrton Lucas; Pulgar, Jorginho, Arrascaeta; Carrascal, Pedro, Samuel Lino. Manager: Leonardo Jardim.

Athletico Paranaense possible starting lineup:

Santos; Benavidez, Aguirre, Esquivel; Gilberto, Luiz Gustavo, Jadson, Mendoza; Bruno Zapelli, Joao Cruz, Kerwin Vargas. Manager: Odair Hellmann.

Athletico's task would have been difficult enough as it is, but with their top scorer and best defender both unavailable, it is hard to see the visitors taking anything from this encounter.

For Flamengo, the priority will be to maintain their formidable home record and head into the most eagerly anticipated game of the year in a favourable position. A convincing victory at the Maracana would be the ideal way to achieve that.
