#1874. Wayne Rooney's suicide admission 'massive' for footballers everywhere, says Bradford City manager

That was the word Michael Duff used to describe Wayne Rooney's contribution to football this week.

Because one of the great players of his generation, England's most capped outfielder and top goalscorer until Harry Kane took both records, has spoken about considering taking his own life when at the peak of career with Manchester United.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Some seem to think that the obscene amounts players of Rooney's profile get paid makes them immune to psychological problems, insulated against off-field issues and fair game for any criticism going. That argument even seems to extend down the pyramid to those not earning small fortunes, but still lucky enough to be earning a living in a game many of us would have dearly loved to be paid to play.

Even when 48-year-old Duff was a player, in the Premier League with Burnley and at international level with Northern Ireland, that lack of empathy towards players dealing with personal or even physical issues was rife in the game as well as outside of it.

But now Rooney has gone public, Duff can tell the players now under his charge, at League One Bradford City, they should not suffer in shamed silence.

“I think we just see a superstar earning £300,000 a week or whatever he's earning and you think it must be all right for him,” says former Barnsley and Huddersfield Town manager Duff.

“I can assure you none of our lads are earning £300,000 a week but they've all got their own lives as well.

“There's a lot more exposure now, with social media and things – they're all on it.

“You have to give up a lot and it's easy to fall into (depression) particularly when you are injured, a long-term one, and you see all your mates going out onto the training pitch. It's all you want to do.

“So we have to help players and educate them.”

Duff thinks Rooney's admission – albeit long after he retired – can help to educate those within the game.

“I played with Clarke Carlisle (at Burnley), who tried to kill himself,” recalls Duff. “You look back and you think I probably should have spotted something there.

“But it was all banter or 'The state of him,' that sort of thing.

“It was probably a cry for help but you didn't know at the time because you weren't educated.

“So for someone at that level to come out and say that about the height of his fame playing at the top, top, top level...

“That's sort of almost like the release is the football pitch. They just want to play football because that's where they're at the happiest.

“So I think it's really good what he's done. I think it's important with the education.”

And it is not just the approach to mental issues where Duff sees a vast improvement when it comes to the well-being of footballers.

“In the old days, it was just 'Get on with it' – injuries and concussions, all those sort of things,” he argues.

“The manager would tell the doctor, 'He ain't coming off' and the player's like, 'I ain't coming off.'

“It's irrelevant what the player thinks any more. It's the safeguarding of the players. It is really important.”

And social media can be a release for the jealousy of others with footballers in their sights.

“Part of the job is you get a stick and abuse,” acknowledges Duff. “Sometimes it goes too far.

“Everyone's got an opinion but you're not allowed to have one back (as a footballer). They are human beings.

“I don't go on social media. I don't need to. If we win, someone will say good things, if we don't, they won't.

“But it's when it starts getting personal it's a slightly different thing.

“And there's other pressures that people don't see.

“They see putting a shirt on and playing in front of 20,000, which is amazing but there's loads of other pressures within that. Whether it's money or whether it's providing for a family or looking after an ill parent or something like that.”

What brought Duff onto the topic of mental health in football was a first serious injury of his career for 22-year-old Bantams forward Bobby Pointon, who is not expected to play again in 2026 because of a knee problem.

Where once you would hear stories of even managerial greats refusing to even acknowledge the presence of injured players at the training ground, now football is super-focused on looking after them mentally.

“Hopefully it's not as bad as what we think,” comments Duff. “But we're in that sort of don't-know situation at the minute.

“It's his first (serious injury) so part of his education is learning what to do, how to live when you're injured.

“We need to help him and educate him to get through these periods because he just wants to play football.

“It underlines the importance of the topic.”

#1870. Exclusive: Charlton boss Nathan Jones among managers objecting to FA rule change

Charlton manager Nathan Jones is among a number of head coaches in English football’s top four divisions to have objected to the reduction in how many yellow cards leads to a touchline ban.

Standard Sport understands that at a recent managers’ meeting, Jones and other head coaches from clubs among the 92 argued a 2023 change in FA rules towards stricter punishments for technical-area misconduct remains unjustified at a time when football managers have never faced greater pressure and volatility.

It is the view of some managers, including Jones, that the FA’s move to bring forward touchline bans from four yellow cards to three is incongruous with an increasingly demanding working environment.

Head coaches across the Premier League and EFL are understood to have this season been shown research that suggests managers’ behaviour usually improves once they reach three bookings.

Managers are regularly reminded of a variety of regulations including technical-area misconduct rules during meetings with the FA’s disciplinary teams, who often present research and statistics to contextualise changes to rules or emerging trends.

Ahead of the 2018-19 season, new rules were introduced to clean up touchline behaviour. Managers across the FA Cup, EFL, Carabao Cup, EFL Trophy and National League could receive yellow and red cards for the first time, with four yellows resulting in a one-match touchline ban.

It is the view of some managers, including Jones, that the FA’s move to bring forward touchline bans from four yellow cards to three is unreasonable

Premier League managers would receive only verbal cautions for “irresponsible behaviour” but then the top flight fell in line with the same level of punishment from 2019-20 onwards.

A further update was made ahead of the 2023-24 campaign when the FA launched a new ‘Participant Behaviour Charter’ as part of its ‘Love Football, Protect the Game’ campaign, developed alongside the Premier League, EFL, Women's Super League, Women's Championship, National League System (Steps 1–4), and PGMOL (now Pro Ref), with input from the League Managers Association (LMA) and Professional Footballers' Association (PFA).

The charter’s aim was to improve the image of the game and maintain a positive environment. Four yellows for a managerial suspension was reduced to three and has remained so ever since.

A new cut-off for technical-area cautions was introduced this season. Managers who receive their third technical-area booking after the 37th round of EFL league matches do not incur an immediate suspension. At that point an automatic one-match touchline ban is triggered only if a fourth yellow card is picked up in a subsequent game.

Compared with its peak, the number of technical-area cautions issued has decreased by 17 per cent since the introduction of the ‘Participation Behaviour Charter’, FA sources say.

Under the FA’s ‘Laws of the Game’, other staff and substitutes in a technical area can also be cautioned or even sent off.

In certain circumstances, managers and head coaches can get booked or sent off on behalf of the misconduct of others in their technical area if the fourth official reports a situation deserving of punishment to the referee but cannot verify who in the technical area committed the offence. In such situations, FA rules state cards can be shown to the “manager or most senior coach in [the technical] area”.

The Reds have tried to strengthen their hand by agreeing to meet with unhappy supporters but the biggest thing in their favour at Oakwell could be doubts in the minds of the visitors.

For a first League One away game as Owls manager, Dave Challinor would surely like to face a team as down in the dumps as Barnsley.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Only kept off the bottom by Bromley's woeful goal difference, Daniel Stendel's side have not won in the league since September 2, nine matches ago.

Consecutive cup wins in which they put 14 goals past lower-division opposition feel like a mirage after they were put back in their box by Wigan Athletic. Captain Cameron McGeehan was booked, and is suspended for Friday's home game.

With a pre-match protest planned, chairman Neerav Parekh will meet independent supporters groups and the media to try to address the disquiet, but not until Friday December 4, with a wider fans’ forum to follow.

So it all points one way, until you consider the geography.

Because derbies can be great levellers, and more importantly the Owls have a hang-up against opponents from Yorkshire.

In their last 14 such matches, their only victory was a 2-1 win over Middlesbrough on Easter Monday 2025, when Anthony Musaba scored an 89th-minute winner.

Much of the squad played no part in many of those defeats, and last season's matches against Boro, Hull City and Sheffield United can be written off, so handicapped were the Owls.

But the pattern has continued this season in a division they are expected to be strong in.

Bradford City inflicted their first defeat back in League One with an August 1-0 win which flattered the beaten hosts.

And points dropped against Huddersfield Town and Doncaster Rovers were nails in manager Henrik Pedersen's coffin.

It took a late fightback and a Terriers implosion for Wednesday to escape with a 2-2 draw from a game Martin Drury's side had much the better of for all but the last few minutes.

If that amplified doubts about Pedersen's management, Doncaster's third and at present last league win of the campaign, 2-0 at home to the Owls, confirmed them in the eyes of the board.

The angry away fans who chanted "You're getting sacked in the morning" were right.

It shows how psychological hurdles like this can outlive personnel changes on the field and in the dugout.

It should not have much bearing on Friday, but most probably will. And with four White Rose teams for company in League One, it is a bad division for any Yorkshire team to have a derby hang-up in.

On the more positive side, win in front of a packed away end which can be heard loud and clear in the tunnel and it will go a long way towards forging the bonds Challinor needs to make the most of Wednesday's biggest asset – their fanbase.

But if Barnsley can play on their derby insecurity, a home win would do wonders at the best time of the season to find some momentum.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel has voted unanimously that Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty against Hull.

The Gunners beat Hull 1-0 in the final match before the international break to go five points clear at the top of the Premier League.

However, it could have been a much more comfortable afternoon had Arsenal been given a penalty in the first half, when it was still goalless.

Kai Havertz went down in the box as he made a run in behind, having been pulled back by Nobel Mendy.

It was not initially seen by the officials but VAR advised the referee to stop play and consult the pitchside monitor.

Farai Hallam deemed that while Havertz had been fouled, he was in an offside position and therefore a free-kick was given to Hull.

The KMI panel have now confirmed that was the incorrect decision due to the foul taking place before Havertz became active.

All five members of the group voted that both the on-field decision and the outcome of the VAR intervention was wrong.

“Although Havertz is clearly in an offside position, there is a clear and impactful holding action by Mendy before any potential offside offence by Havertz,” the panel explained.

“Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded. The panel considered the VAR intervention was correct; however, the outcome after the on-field review was considered to be incorrect as a penalty should have been awarded.”

The panel added: “Being in an offside position, in itself, is not an offence.

“IFAB Law 11 says that a player in an offside position at the moment the ball is played or touched by a team-mate is only penalised on becoming involved in active play.

“If a player is fouled before becoming involved in active play, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence. Therefore, in this instance, Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty.”

Following that fixture in Cincinnati, Pochettino flew straight to Manchester, then headed to the Red Devils' Carrington training complex.

Club legend Michael Carrick was sacked after winning just one of 10 top-flight fixtures this season.

#1862. Troyes vs Le Havre - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 18 Nov 2026 02:01

The bottom two teams in Ligue 1 will kick off matchday 11 of the campaign Friday as Troyes welcome Le Havre to Stade de l’Aube

Heading into this match, Troyes are 17th in the table after suffering a narrow 1-0 defeat at Paris Saint-Germain, putting them six points above the Normandy club, who lost their last league fixture 2-0 at home to Lorient.

Some improved results of late have brought Troyes back within reach of Ligue 1 safety after 10 matchdays in the top flight.

After losing five successive matches in this competition, Stephane Dumont has seen his side earn points in two of their last three contests.

One of the biggest improvements has been their poise at the back, as they have collected two clean sheets in their last three league fixtures after conceding multiple goals in five straight games.

While their defensive game is much improved, they are still struggling to create many scoring opportunities, sitting dead last in the league for big chances so far.

On Friday, they can claim consecutive Ligue 1 triumphs at Stade de l’Aube for the first time since March-April 2022, after beating Le Mans on Halloween (2-0).

ESTAC have won three of their last four home meetings with Le Havre, all in Ligue 2, and have lost just one of their last five games against them.

It is an urgent time for Le Havre, who enter this matchday six points back of Ligue 1 safety and are the only side yet to win this season.

The club have said that this is an emergency situation and, as such, appointed Valerien Ismael as the new manager in hopes of getting out of the relegation zone.

The well-travelled coach, who was born in Strasbourg, has a reputation for turning clubs around quickly, taking Barnsley from a team near the bottom of the Championship to a playoff position by the end of the 2020-21 campaign.

Ismael has a big job ahead of him, to transform a side in Le Havre, who have given up the joint-second-most goals in Ligue 1 thus far (22).

He takes over a team that have suffered six consecutive defeats in this competition, while earning just one point away from home this season.

While they have not fared well against Troyes of late, Le Ciel et Marine are unbeaten against them in Ligue 1 this century, winning that last meeting in Normandy in 2003 (1-0).

Due to an ankle injury, Troyes are expected to be without Anis Ouzenadji on Friday, and Yacouba Kone is dealing with a sore knee.

From matchday nine to 10, we saw two new faces in their starting 11, with Ismael Boura and Kandet Diawara replacing Paolo Gozzi and Timothe Nkada, while Hillel Konate got the start between the sticks yet again.

As for Le Havre, Rassoul Ndiaye and Elias Jelert are doubtful because of leg injuries, while Timothee Pembele is dealing with adductor pain and unlikely to feature.

Lionel Mpasi and Felix Mambimbi are out with Achilles tendon ruptures, while Stephan Zagadou is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Konate; Maronnier, Monfray, Diaz, Boura; Mille, Karim, Diop; Le Douaron, Ripart, Nkada

Bodart; Sasso, Koffi, Touba; Ouziad, Ebonog, Mwanga, Richardson; Fofana, Samatta; Maja

Ismael has a reputation for elevating his teams quickly, and against a Troyes side that are not terribly potent in front of goal, we believe the Normandy club will catch a break and pull out a narrow victory.

“I’d keep Bruno [Fernandes], I’d keep Kobbie [Mainoo], I’d keep [Youri] Tielemans, [Mason] Mount would have to go.

“[Andrey] Santos - Mauricio may like him because he’s young, quite mobile, he’s aggressive, he might get something out of him. Him and [Carlos] Baleba will be in that middle bit. Mount’s the one that goes definitely, in that midfield section.”

#1858. Mbappe should not be expected to defend, claims Real Madrid team-mate Rudiger

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Antonio Rudiger is baffled by criticism over Kylian Mbappe's defensive work rate.

Indeed, Rudiger feels it would be unfair to ask Mbappe, one of world football's great goalscorers, to "do my job".

Mbappe has already scored 17 goals and laid on three assists for Real Madrid this season. Of players in Europe's top five leagues, only Barcelona's Raphinha (19) has netted more goals this term.

"Does it make sense for me to ask a man who has scored more than 80 or 90 goals in two years, and has now reached 100 goals for the club, to do my job? That makes no sense," Rudiger told The Athletic.

Rudiger then compared Mbappe to some star forwards of Madrid's recent past.

#1857. Liverpool transfer news: £21m Lamine Camara 'confirmed' to be on radar as Andoni Iraola faces major midfield problem

By Lewis Nolan | 18 Nov 2026 02:09

Liverpool want to sign Athletic Club midfielder Mikel Jauregizar, who is seen as an alternative to Lamine Camara, the newest report has claimed.

The Merseysiders are preparing to take on rivals Manchester United on Sunday, and victory will be key for the club's pursuit of a place in Premier League's top four.

If Andoni Iraola's side are to get the better of the Red Devils, they will need to win the midfield battle, though that has been an area of concern for some time.

Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai have often disappointed in the middle of the pitch, and that has led to calls for reinforcements.

While Liverpool have strongly been credited interest in Monaco star Camara, Anfield Watch have now claimed that the Reds also have Athletic Bilbao's Jauregizar on their list of targets.

Valued at just under £21m by Transfermarkt, Jauregizar would likely not command as high a fee as Camara, which would make a January move more realistic.

The 23-year-old has only started three La Liga games this season, featuring in seven, and he has won 51% of his duels in the top flight.

Jauregizar only won 47% of his duels in the league in 2025-26, but his struggles in that regard are not shared with Camara, who has won 66% of his duels this campaign in Ligue 1.

The Monaco midfielder is also more accomplished with the ball, and he should still be seen as the premium option, either in January or the summer.

Trey Nyoni will almost certainly become a starter in the next few years, and signing another midfielder would pose a problem in terms of guaranteeing playing time.

Szoboszlai and Gravenberch are contracted to Anfield until 2031 and 2032 respectively, so moving on either player would be difficult.

Alexis Mac Allister has been the Reds' best midfielder this season and has arguably been among the best performers in that role across the division, so losing him in the coming summer would weaken the squad.

Liverpool may soon be faced with a painful decision, with at least one of their established stars likely to head for the exit doors in the coming months.

#1856. Luis de la Fuente singles out ‘fantastic’ England star after Spain defeat

Luis de la Fuente reserved special praise for James Trafford following Spain’s 3-2 defeat to England, hailing the goalkeeper’s ‘fantastic’ display in Madrid.

England produced arguably their finest all-round performance under Thomas Tuchel in Sunday’s Nations League classic to land a hefty psychological blow on the reigning world and European champions.

The Three Lions flew out of the blocks from minute one and were duly rewarded for their efforts as captain Harry Kane converted from the spot to break the deadlock on the stroke of half-time.

Goals from Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased the deficit after the restart, with Spain all at sea before Elliot Anderson’s sending off handed the hosts a lifeline.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored with the resulting penalty before Nico Williams finished off a flowing Spanish move to set up a tense final 15 minutes at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But ten-man England managed to keep La Roja at bay thanks largely to an inspired Trafford, who was selected over Jordan Pickford and repaid Tuchel’s faith with a series of stunning late stops to help preserve the visitors’ narrow advantage

Trafford’s double save to keep out Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte earned the Leeds United keeper immediate high fives and adulation from his team-mates.

The result brought Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten streak to a halt and ensured England finished top of their Nations League group having picked up 15 from a possible 18 points.

‘Positives? There are a lot of positives to find here. It’s very difficult to get here, to achieve the numbers that we’ve achieved,’ Spain boss De La Fuente said when asked about Spain’s run being brought to an end.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It’s something historical that we’ve done. We’ve been champions of the Nations League, the Euros, the World Cup, everything is positive.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘But we know how to win and we know how to lose. And we have to say that we faced a rival that we managed to beat in the past but I have to say that they were the better team in the first 30 minutes.

‘I had a feeling we could get there when they went one man down but I’m really proud of this team, their hunger, their eagerness.

‘I’m convinced that the best is yet to come for this team.’

De la Fuente made four second-half substitutions as they looked to claw their way back into the contest, with Fermin Lopez, Nico Williams, Pedri and Dean Huijsen all sent on in the Spanish capital.

But the home team were thwarted by Trafford’s heroics in the closing stages – and De la Fuente took the opportunity to applaud the ‘keeper’s outstanding showing.

‘What we wanted to do with the substitutions was try to go all out, try to generate more chances,’ he explained.

‘We did generate some chances but England’s goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last ten or 15 minutes.

‘In any case, there were many alternatives but again, I want to say how fantastic England were on the night.’

Asked what he and Tuchel had discussed shortly after the final whistle, De La Fuente replied: ‘We just spoke for a few seconds about what happened this week and we just wanted to clarify things.

‘I have no problem with him at all, all I have is admiration and respect.

‘As for the dressing room, when you are not used to losing, you look at eachother and ask, “What happened here?”, so what did I tell my players? I told them that we haven’t lost for three years and we’ve won all the important tournaments.

‘All I wanted to do was say how proud I am of them because of this and it’s a shame we don’t have another game coming up, we have to wait until March.’

The Spain head coach added: ‘We’ll surely come back in March with renewed energy, thinking about the Nations League final.

‘We’re going to try to get there, knowing difficult it is to get there and win a competition like this.

‘But the spirit, the intention, the ambition are all there.’

#1855. Nations League quarter-final draw simulated: England get favourable tie as Spain handed France rematch

The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals is now just days away, and England's route to potential international glory will become clearer.

Following the conclusion of an exciting and unpredictable group phase, the stage has been set as seven teams aim to dethrone two-time winners Portugal next summer.

The holders are safely through to the knockout phase as group winners, but they only confirmed their position on the final matchday after beating Wales in a five-goal thriller in Cardiff.

Joining Portugal in progressing from Group A4 are Norway following a remarkable comeback against Denmark on Tuesday night.

Trailing 2-0 after just 14 minutes, a brace from Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard gave the World Cup quarter-finalists a 3-2 win as they pipped the Danes to the runners-up spot by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

There was also final matchday drama in England’s group. Thomas Tuchel’s side travelled to Madrid needing to beat reigning world and European champions Spain to top Group A3 and did exactly that, despite playing the last half hour with 10-men.

Netherlands lost out on top spot to Germany in Group A2 after being thumped 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp’s side, but squeezed through on goal difference having finished level on points with Greece.

France and Belgium have qualified from Group A1, meaning seven of the top 11 ranked teams in the world have made it through to the Nations League quarter-finals.

So ahead of Friday's draw, who will be paired with who? Well, the four seeded sides each have three possibilities as teams from the same group cannot be paired with each other.

As a result, a knockout stage simulator has determined their potential opponents in the quarter-final and it's safe to say the results are quite fascinating.

In this simulation, England have been paired with the Netherlands in what would be a repeat of the semi-final during the inaugural season of the Nations League.

While the Three Lions were beaten on that occasion, it would be a favourable draw given they have won two of the last three meetings against the Dutch - including the Euro 2024 semi-final.

The simulator hasn't been as kind to France as they've been paired with Spain, a team they have lost to three times in a row since victory in the 2021 final.

In addition, the simulator has thrown up two other eye-catching fixtures with Norway taking on Germany, and Portugal continuing the defence of their crown against Belgium over two legs.

#1854. Thomas Tuchel speaks out on James Trafford vs Jordan Pickford battle for England spot

Thomas Tuchel insists that England do not have a number one, after James Trafford made a brilliant case to be first choice goalkeeper in the win over Spain.

Trafford played the full game as the Three Lions pulled off a memorable 3-2 Nations League win over the world champions in Madrid.

It was a stunning first hour from Tuchel’s side and the visitors were 3-0 up on 57 minutes thanks to goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

Things started to unravel a bit from there as Elliot Anderson was shown a straight red card and Mikel Oyarzabal converted from the penalty spot.

Nico Williams then made it a very nervy climax for England as he scored on 75 minutes and the hosts pushed for an equaliser.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Trafford helped his team stand firm, though, including making a tremendous double save late on.

Everton’s Jordan Pickford has been first choice goalkeeper since 2018, winning 94 caps, but his place is now in doubt thanks to the emergence of Trafford.

James Trafford last-gasp double save 🤯🤯#UNLSaves | @Betano_PT pic.twitter.com/K3Rn995OEE

Tuchel was not ready to declare either stopper his number one, but was clearly very impressed by the Leeds United star.

‘There’s no number one,’ said the England boss. ‘It’s a good double save. That’s what we wanted. He had a brilliant match. It only works if you’re top from number one to 11.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Tuchel continued on Trafford: ‘Very good. That’s his job, to close the gap. We want competition in all positions. We need to see Trafford in high-pressure moments.

‘The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end. Absolutely brilliant.’

The German has also liked what he has seen from Trafford on the ball, saying: ‘There was a lot to do in the deep build-up as well, which he did very, very well, with everyone around him.

‘Never lose the concentration, never lose the focus, never lose the vision where to find the free men to overcome the press and put the game to the opponent’s half.

‘With everyone else, he was part of a fantastic team performance.’

At 24 years old, Trafford is eight years younger than Pickford and looks to be his successor, even if he has not entirely displaced him just yet.

The win in Spain meant England topped their Nations League group and will play a runner-up from another group in the quarter-finals of the competition.

Groups A2 and A4 come to an end on Monday and Tuesday respectively, which is when we will learn England’s possible opponents for Friday’s draw.

Belgium have already secured second place in group A1, so they are a possible opponent for the Three Lions in the quarter-finals that are played in March next year.

#1853. Capello pays tribute to Baresi and is ‘waiting for results’ after Cardinale’s bold claims

Fabio Capello recalled what Franco Baresi meant to him as a player and captain, while commenting on Gerry Cardinale’s bold declarations too.

Few players mean more to a club – if any – than Baresi meant to Milan. The centre-back reinvented the role and became a symbol of one of the most dominant eras in the history of the sport, as well as an icon in the eyes of the fans who adored him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Capello was lucky enough to coach the No.6 and he spoke about Baresi’s greatness on Andrea Longoni’s YouTube channel ‘Milan Hello’. His words were relayed by MilanNews, and the emotion was clear in his voice.

#1852. Premier League predictions: Standard Sport names title winners, relegation race, Golden Boot and more

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The 2026-27 Premier League season is just days away from resumption following the final international break of the year, and with it the return of some familiar faces.

Mauricio Pochettino is back in English football after a spell in international management, he has succeeded Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach. Meanwhile, Thomas Frank has replaced Pierre Sage at Crystal Palace.

After 10 games of the campaign, both Man United and Palace are in the relegation zone. So will these appointment help to drag them out of the bottom three?

At the other end of the table, Arsenal have made a solid start to the defence of their Premier League crown, and appear to have a surprise challenger as confusion has set in around Manchester City.

Plenty of questions to be answered over the next six months, and the Standard Sport football reporters, Matt Verri, Dom Smith and Sam Tabuteau, have had a go at predicting what is in store for the remainder of the season.

MV: Arsenal continue to look ruthlessly efficient and should be confident of defending their title. The defensive unit is absurdly good, the midfield depth is ridiculous, and it means the forwards only need to deliver a moment or two per match.

Even whey they are not at their best, Arsenal are just so difficult to beat. That is the case over 90 minutes and it should be the case over 38 matches again.

DS: No reason to change what I predicted at the beginning of the season, which was for Arsenal to win the Premier League title. If anything, the opening 10 rounds of games have made me more convinced the Gunners won’t be caught and will defend last season’s crown.

Arsenal fans may continue to worry about a lack of goals from their forwards, but their defence is on track to perform even better than last season’s, and that gives other challengers a daunting task to catch them. Arsenal could genuinely win the title by as many as 15 points.

ST: Arsenal were favourites to retain the Premier League title before the season started and that has not changed 10 games in.

Chelsea have the firepower in attack to secure fourth and Unai Emery can work his magic to get Aston Villa into fifth.

Sunderland, Forest and Coventry will be the three to go down.

Joao Pedro would be the one I might have backed to challenge him, but injury has stalled his challenge.

DS: Why would it be anyone other than Erling Haaland? It says a lot that even after the Norwegian was criticised in some circles for failing to score in City’s last two league games, the defeats to Brighton and Nottingham Forest, he is still sitting pretty on top of the leaderboard with nine goals in 10 league games.

The Golden Boot simply won’t be won by anyone else.

#1851. Arsenal transfer news: David Ornstein drops interesting update on Eli Junior Kroupi ahead of January

By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 06:57

Arsenal could face imminent disappointment in their pursuit of AFC Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, with David Ornstein providing an update on the 19-year-old's future.

The Gunners have been monitoring the Frenchman after his impressive performances, but a move for him in the January transfer window is now looking increasingly unlikely.

Ornstein has also suggested that Kroupi could favour a move away from the Premier League when he eventually leaves the Vitality Stadium.

In a recent The Athletic Q&A, Ornstein downplayed the prospect of the Cherries sanctioning a January departure, saying the club has little financial incentive to sell midway through the campaign.

The forward is under contract until 2030, meaning the Cherries are in a strong negotiating position and can afford to wait until the summer before considering significant offers.

Ornstein also highlighted that Kroupi only made his first appearance of the season on October 25th after an injury lay-off, with Bournemouth keen to benefit from his contributions during the remainder of the campaign.

Perhaps more significantly for Arsenal, the ever-reliable journalist suggested that the teenager could prefer a move abroad rather than another Premier League club.

Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona have both been heavily linked, with Ornstein indicating that the information available to him points towards those destinations being more likely than a move within England.

He did acknowledge that an exceptional financial offer from a Premier League club could change the situation, but his expectation is that Bournemouth would be more receptive to a sale next summer.

Ornstein's update represents a significant complication for Arsenal, who could now need to explore alternative attacking targets if they want to strengthen in January.

Kroupi's contract situation means Bournemouth have little reason to entertain offers, while the player's reported preference for moving abroad further weakens the Gunners' position.

Antonio Nusa could therefore become a more realistic alternative for Gunners boss Mikel Arteta.

The RB Leipzig winger is another young attacking talent attracting Premier League interest, with Arsenal previously linked alongside Tottenham and reportedly confident of competing for his signature.

Nusa would not necessarily provide the same centre-forward option as Kroupi, but his ability to operate out wide could address another area where Arsenal need greater depth.

Ultimately, Kroupi remains an exciting long-term target, but the combination of Bournemouth's stance and his apparent preference for a move abroad suggests Arsenal may have to be patient or turn their attention elsewhere in January.

A stunning comeback victory over Roma followed by a 4-4 thriller at home to Aston Villa in the Premier League were ultimately not enough to save Carrick, who was relieved of his duties last Thursday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach Mauricio Pochettino was subsequently announced as Carrick’s successor, with the Argentine officially vacating his position with the United States national team to start life in the role later this week.

It’s understood the Old Trafford giants will also be in the market for attacking reinforcements on the back of a desperately disappointing start to the season for the likes of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko.

Another high-profile name heavily linked with United in recent weeks has been Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has scored five goals in his opening nine appearances for Leeds this term.

But Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with the Red Devils, believes the England striker would only be brought in as a stop-gap for his former club up front.

‘I think Dominic Calvert-Lewin would be a stop-gap,’ the ex-United and France defender explained.

‘I don’t think it’s a long-term. He doesn’t belong in a Manchester United squad. So I don’t know where this is coming from.

‘Yes, you need to have a look around for strikers because of the Sesko situation with his injury, and we are short in that department, but I wouldn’t consider Calvert-Lewin as an option.’

All eyes will be on Anfield on Sunday when Pochettino takes charge of United for the first time against bitter rivals Liverpool.

Pochettino takes over the reins from Carrick with the club languishing down in 18th place in the Premier League, just point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

#1849. ‘There are different ways of winning’, says Mead after Man City edge out Hacken

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Beth Mead said "there are different ways to win football matches" after Manchester City battled their way to a 2-0 victory over Hacken.

Man City made it back-to-back wins in the Women's Champions League on Wednesday, thanks to second-half goals from Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw.

Andree Jeglertz turned to star attackers Hemp and Shaw at half-time at Nordic Wellness Arena, with City having failed to make the breakthrough in the first period, despite creating chances worth a combined 1.08 expected goals.

Hemp's introduction paid dividends when she opened the scoring in the 55th minute by bundling home while challenging for the ball. She then teed up Shaw to put the result beyond doubt late on, before Mary Fowler missed a stoppage-time penalty.

City finished with 3.43 xG, and while they were not at their clinical best, Mead, who was taken off for Shaw, was more than happy with the performance.

"It was a tough game – we had to work hard for the three points," she told UEFA.

"I'm really proud. It's been a busy schedule. Every player has been bringing different energy to the pitch – a different kind of pitch to play on, obviously. Everybody in the team turned up today and we did what we needed to do.

"There are different ways of winning football matches. Coming away from home in the Champions League is difficult but we found a way to win today."

— Manchester City Women (@ManCityWomen) November 18, 2026

Jeglertz, meanwhile, said City got exactly the game they were expecting.

He told UEFA: "A good game. We knew it would be a tough game to score against a very organised defending team. They have a great goalkeeper and we struggled in first half. In the second half, they got a little bit tired, we got a little more space and we managed to get the goals.

"We try to get the best out of each player and put them in positions where they can really show what qualities they have.

"We have a great team together, we rotate players, and they all have a great impact on what we're doing. I think that will be very important in the future."

City have lost just one of their 11 group stage/league phase games in the Champions League (W6 D3), losing 0-3 to Barcelona in December 2024.

#1848. Pictured: Mauricio Pochettino arrives at airport before starting Manchester United role

Mauricio Pochettino has been pictured arriving in the UK for the first time as Manchester United manager.

The Argentine flew straight from the United States in the early hours of Wednesday morning and the Gulfstream G700 he was believed to be on was spotted landing at Manchester airport shortly before midday.

It was announced last week that the former Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea boss was making a return to the Premier League, succeeding Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

However, the 54-year-old’s start to his fourth spell in English football was delayed as he finished up commitments with the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT), overseeing an 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals in his last game in charge.

Now after touching down in the UK, Pochettino can now take the next step in his career.

“I am ready [to return],” he told the Telegraph. “This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here.

“Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’

“[He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool].

“But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good.

“But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything … this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”

Pochettino is expected to head to Carrington immediately as he settles into his new role as Man United head coach, with the focus already shifting to his first game in charge against Liverpool on Sunday.

#1846. Xabi Alonso facing new Chelsea team selection dilemma after Emi Martinez fitness boost

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso may have a selection headache on his hands after Emi Martinez returned to action.

Martinez played the full 90 minutes as Argentina thumped Costa Rica 7-0, producing two saves in a comfortable outing for what was his first outing since sustaining his jaw injury against Everton.

The goalkeeper had been an unused substitute for Argentina during their 2-1 defeat to Uruguay on Friday, watching on as Manchester City’s Geronimo Rulli got the nod.

Martinez’s return to action may represent a selection headache for Alonso ahead of Chelsea’s Premier League clash against Leeds this weekend.

Mike Penders has impressed during the Argentine’s absence, recovering from a shaky performance in Chelsea’s shock 2-0 loss to Tottenham, to prove dependable and stake claim to be the first-choice option in between the sticks.

Penders has already faced Leeds once this season, keeping goal as the Blues roared back from 2-0 down to win 6-3 in the Carabao Cup third round back in September.

However, the 21-year-old’s run of games for Chelsea was not enough to earn a starting role for Belgium during the international break.

Manchester United’s Senne Lammens kept his place as number one for Belgium, as Penders watched on as victories over Turkey and Italy secured a spot in the Nations League quarter finals.

In total, Martinez missed four Premier League games, with Chelsea winning one, drawing the other, and losing twice.

#1845. Liverpool transfer news: Reds join Barcelona race for Brazilian defender amid Van Dijk doubt

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 07:04

Liverpool have reportedly entered the race with Barcelona to sign a Brazilian gem, with the future of Virgil van Dijk still unresolved. The Dutch defender’s contract runs until the end of the season and he has yet to reach an agreement over an extension, while Liverpool are monitoring the market.

While the January transfer window is yet to open, Liverpool are facing a dilemma behind the scenes. With his contract running until the end of the season, Van Dijk has no renewal agreement in progress and can sign a pre-contract agreement from January.

With the situation of the Dutch defender unresolved, Liverpool have entered the race with Barcelona to sign a Brazilian gem.

According to Sports Illustrated, Liverpool have sent scouts to follow the rise of Arthur Dias closely and are now assessing the possibility of buying him from Athletico Paranaense. The 19-year-old defender is one of the breakout stars of Brazilian football in 2026 and is being watched by several European clubs.

Barcelona’s interest in Arthur Dias is long-standing, as being left-footed and comfortable playing out from the back are qualities missing from manager Hansi Flick’s squad. Van Dijk, who is right-footed but also plays on the left side of central defence, would leave a gap for Liverpool to fill should he depart.

The Brazilian centre-back has a contract until December 2028 and has already seen a Tottenham Hotspur offer of £18m (€21m) rejected by Athletico Paranaense. The club’s board believes Arthur Dias should only be released for an offer of at least £25.5m (€30m) because of his high potential.

So far, Liverpool have made no formal approach to Athletico Paranaense for the young defender, but the competition is not limited to Barcelona.

Clubs such as Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are also monitoring Arthur Dias, who gained international visibility with his first two call-ups to the Brazil national team in the post-World Cup international breaks.

Brazilian aside, Liverpool’s number four has no guaranteed future at Anfield. Despite his idol status and undisputed place in the starting line-up under manager Andoni Iraola, Van Dijk has no advanced talks with the club’s directors over his stay, with moves towards an extension expected to gather pace at the turn of the year.

The captain himself admitted in a recent interview that he plans to stay at Liverpool, but has no news on his situation.

The Spanish manager is in favour of Van Dijk staying, as the Dutchman is not only a leadership figure in the dressing room but also a pillar of the defensive system, having won 75% of his duels in this season’s Premier League.

In that context, AC Milan have emerged as one of the clubs interested in the 35-year-old defender. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is an admirer of the Dutchman and believes he can make a difference to Ruben Amorim’s project through his experience and technical quality.

#1844. Martin Zubimendi stance on Chelsea transfer as Arsenal set asking price

Martin Zubimendi is seriously considering leaving Arsenal for the first time and has refused to rule out a move to Chelsea, according to reports in Spain.

Zubimendi is yet to start a Premier League game for Arsenal this season, with the concerning lack of game-time sparking speculation over his future at the Emirates Stadium.

The Spanish midfielder enjoyed a bright start to his Gunners career following a £60m move from Real Sociedad, earning rave reviews from Mikel Arteta this time last year.

But Zubimendi had lost his place in the Arsenal team by the end of the season, with a teenage Myles Lewis-Skelly instead starting the Champions League final against PSG.

The 27-year-old has continued to struggle for minutes this season and is now, for the first time, considering his future at the club.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Spanish outlet AS say Zubimendi has his eye on a January exit and is ‘open to everything’ following reports linking him with Chelsea, Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid.

Xabi Alonso is keen to strengthen his midfield options and knows Zubimendi well from his previous spell at Real Sociedad.

Zubimendi is contracted to Arsenal until 2030 but reports in Spain say the north London club will consider offers for the World Cup winner of at least £60m.

Last week, Zubimendi was forced to address speculation linking him with a move away from Arsenal while on international duty with Spain.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too,’ he told Marca. ‘I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumours can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

‘Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

‘Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens.

‘I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.’

Zubimendi also revealed he was warned about a possible lack of minutes by Arteta ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

Arteta bolstered his midfield options over the summer, with Arsenal spending £75m to sign Brazil international Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United.

‘I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season,’ Zubimendi added. ‘As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me.

‘He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

‘I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players.

‘I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time. I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation.

‘It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too. Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

‘I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side.

‘I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.’

#1842. Manchester United urged to target ‘established Premier League leader’ as Bruno Fernandes replacement

Former Manchester United winger Ashley Young has revealed he would replace Bruno Fernandes with Nottingham Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

Fernandes's contract expires at the end of this season, though United can extend their captain’s deal by an additional year and also prevent him from speaking to foreign clubs in January about a potential free transfer.

United want Fernandes to stay, but the 32-year-old has already turned down two new contract proposals as he weighs up his options following more managerial turnover at Old Trafford.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of his first training session on Wednesday after leaving the US men’s national team to replace Michael Carrick as United head coach.

Fernandes enjoyed a superb campaign last term, breaking the single-season Premier League assist record to help United qualify for the Champions League.

This season, however, he has struggled to replicate the same form, and he drew criticism after calling into question Carrick’s tactics following United’s 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como in October.

While Young admits there is no doubt about Fernandes’ contribution to United, with the Portuguese midfielder producing 75 goals and 74 assists in 239 Premier League appearances, he insists that in order for the Red Devils to move on, they should look to replace the former Sporting man with England international Gibbs-White.

“Bruno has been fantastic for Manchester United. He has been, and no one can say that he hasn’t,” Young tells Standard Sport.

“There's obviously been a few things that have come up of late. If a club like Manchester United are going to build a team around him, he's going to be 33 next year.

“If it was me, I would be looking at going to get another number 10 and build it around him. I'd go and get Morgan Gibbs-White.

“I think he's got 18 months left on his contract. He's established in the Premier League, he’s a leader, he's showing his qualities at Nottingham Forest. And I'm sure Nottingham Forest won't thank me for saying that.”

#1841. Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman smashes Jude Bellingham England Under-21 record

Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman has broken two England Under-21 records previously held by Jude Bellingham in a matter of days.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player ever to play for the Three Lions at Under-21 level when he came off the bench on Friday in a 1-0 defeat to Portugal.

Dowman then started against France at Aston Gate on Monday night, scoring a dramatic late winner in a 3-2 victory.

His appearance against Portugal broke Bellingham’s record as youngest England Under-21 player and his goal against France broke the Real Madrid superstar’s record as youngest to score at this level.

Dowman was 16 years and 320 days when he scored in Bristol on Monday, while Bellingham was 17 years and 67 days old when he made his debut against Kosovo in 2020, scoring on his first appearance for England Under-21s.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Also on the scoresheet for England in the friendly win over France were Tottenham’s Mikey Moore and Manchester City’s Divin Mubama, who is on loan at Southampton this season.

Manchester City’s Rico Lewis captained Lee Carsley’s side, while the likes of Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood and Liverpool’s Trey Nyoni were also in the starting XI.

It was Dowman who was making yet more history, though, having already become the youngest player to score in the Premier League and to make an appearance in the Champions League.

When Arsenal won the title last season, he also became the youngest player to lift the Premier League trophy.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The incredible talent does not turn 17 until December 31 and will hope to get more run outs for Arsenal before then, although he has only had one very brief substitute appearance for the Gunners since his red card against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on October 27.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was clearly fuming with Dowman when he was shown a straight red card for reacting to a heavy challenge against Fleetwood, giving the youngster stern words as he left the field.

Arteta said: ‘I haven’t seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it is positive or negative. But you need to understand the context and the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

‘But, I don’t know. You can have another reaction. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me some days you might say “I don’t like the reaction”. For me, it was the best reaction to be who I am.’

He added: ‘The reaction when I don’t win, you want to know what my reaction is? I am [angry] big time.

‘So, we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality, otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League and this level.

‘We look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time we are going to demand from him, like everybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Because the other boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair.’

The announcement follows reports of an agreement in October, when Arsenal and Manchester City were credited with earlier interest in the midfielder. Those reports suggested a deal running until at least 2031; Madrid has now confirmed the expiry date as 2032. The club has not disclosed the financial terms.

#1839. Chelsea and Manchester United lead tributes as Juan Mata announces football retirement

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea and Manchester United led the tributes to Juan Mata after he announced his retirement from professional football.

The former Spain international, who lifted the 2010 World Cup and 2012 European Championship, has hung up his boots at the age of 38 after leaving Australian giants Melbourne Victory in September.

Mata started his career at Real Madrid’s academy before moving to Valencia in 2007, where he won the 2008 Copa del Rey alongside fellow future World Cup winners David Silva and David Villa.

He moved to Chelsea in 2011 and helped the Blues win the Champions League and FA Cup in his first season at the club. The diminutive midfielder was crowned Chelsea’s Player of the Year in both of his two full seasons in west London before leaving for Manchester United in January 2014.

Mata helped United win the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup before his departure in 2022. He then spent the latter years of his career with Turkish side Galatasaray and Vissel Kobe in Japan before he played for Australian sides Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory.

Mata announced his retirement with a 50-second video posted on his social media channels.

In the video, Mata sits in a changing room, staring at a pair of football boots. He then turns around and hangs them up on a peg, with the caption: “Sometimes to love is to let go. Thanks, football.”

A full statement was also posted on Mata’s official website, in which he admitted “Football will never leave my life” and that he would continue to use football “as a vehicle for development.”

Mata is best known for co-founding Common Goal, a global movement in which players, coaches, and clubs pledge at least 1% of their salaries to fund grassroots football charities.

“I was able to keep going for so many years because of the sheer joy of playing. Waking up every morning looking forward to training and playing, whether at magnificent grounds such as Old Trafford, Stamford Bridge or Mestalla.

“Or back when I was starting out at Juventud Estadio, where the pitch turned into a mud bath every winter. I believe that kind of passion is fundamental to everything in life.

Man Utd urged to target ‘established leader’ as Bruno Fernandes replacement

Xabi Alonso facing new Chelsea dilemma after Emi Martinez fitness boost

Mauricio Pochettino arrives at airport before starting Man Utd role

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

“Over time, I realised football was about more than just kicking a ball. As I grew older, travelled and lived in different countries, I came to understand the power of sport in general, and football in particular, to change people’s lives.

“Football will never leave my life. There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development. I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer.”

Manchester United paid tribute to Mata, who scored 51 goals in 285 games for the Red Devils, with a post on social media.

“Great player, better person. Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan,” they wrote on social media.

Chelsea also posted a tribute to Mata on their social media pages.

“What a player,” Chelsea wrote in response to his retirement announcement.

#1838. Man Utd full-back facing major contract decision as Mauricio Pochettino plots defensive overhaul

By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 07:17, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 07:17

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing to make several changes to his Manchester United squad, with the defence expected to be a major priority over the coming transfer windows.

Noussair Mazraoui is among those whose long-term future at Old Trafford remains uncertain, despite previously being highly regarded by the club.

The Argentine is keen to assess the Morocco international in person before deciding whether to make a new contract a priority.

Mazraoui is attracting interest from clubs in both Italy and Saudi Arabia, but Pochettino wants to take a closer look at the right-back over the coming weeks before reaching a verdict on his future, according to new reports.

The 29-year-old is contracted to United until the summer of 2028, with the club also holding an option to extend his deal by a further year.

Consequently, neither party is in immediate danger of running out of time to agree fresh terms, and there is no urgency to conclude negotiations.

However, Mazraoui has endured an injury-disrupted start to the campaign, making just five Premier League appearances so far.

United are understood to be planning a 'defensive overhaul' across the next few transfer windows, although the former Bayern Munich defender could avoid the significant changes expected elsewhere in the backline.

His versatility is a major asset, having featured at right-back, left-back and centre-back, while he remains viewed as a potentially important part of the project at Old Trafford.

Nevertheless, Mazraoui will need to impress Pochettino before the manager decides whether to commit to him for the longer term.

United's defensive problems have plagued the club for several seasons, and simply making one or two adjustments is unlikely to provide the necessary solution.

Pochettino, therefore, needs to take a wider view of the backline, with multiple additions potentially required across the defensive positions.

Left-back should be a particularly important area of focus, while further reinforcements at centre-back and right-back could also be needed depending on who survives the anticipated overhaul.

Mazraoui's ability to cover several positions could make him a useful squad member, but his injury record and contract situation mean that his future cannot be taken for granted.

Ultimately, Pochettino must establish which defenders can form part of his long-term plans before United commit significant resources to rebuilding their defence.

#1836. England’s Ivan Toney fails in bid to move assault trial over Euro 2028 clash

Get our award-winning daily news email featuring exclusive stories, opinion and expert analysis

Ivan Toney’s bid to move the date of his assault trial to avoid clashing with Euro 2028 games has been refused by a judge.

The England footballer, 30, hopes to be selected to play for the national side in the next European Championship after featuring in this summer’s World Cup .

Toney is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during a confrontation at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London, on December 6, 2025.

He denied assault occasioning actual bodily harm at a court hearing last month and a date for a three- to four-day trial was fixed for June 12, 2028, which is three days into the Uefa Euro 2028 tournament.

Bid to move footballer Ivan Toney’s trial date to avoid Euro 2028 clash refused

At a hearing at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday, which Toney did not attend, his barrister Mozammel Hossain KC said: “It came to our attention that… there may be potentially a football match called the European championships in 2028 between June 9 and July 9.”

Mr Hossain proposed a trial date in August that year, adding: “We ask you please that the matter be put back to then for a trial so that if the defendant is included in this football tournament he can play.

“My knowledge of football is very limited but I am told he was included in the last one in 2024 and the England squad for the World Cup.”

Judge Tony Baumgartner called it a “speculative” application.

He refused the request, saying: “It does not seem to me to be in the interest of justice to disturb the date that was already fixed.”

The judge said the application could be made again if Toney is selected for the England squad.

An earlier hearing was told the alleged assault happened at the 100 Wardour Street club during a confrontation between the defendant and Mr Da Silva.

It was heard the two men “squared up to each other”, before Toney allegedly “lunged forward and headbutted the complainant, followed by a few punches”.

The Metropolitan Police investigated and the footballer was charged in late July.

Toney, of Northampton, has made 10 international appearances and scored one goal.

He missed out on the latest squad for the country’s Nations League ties.

Toney started his football career with Northampton Town and played for teams including Wigan Athletic and Peterborough United before signing for Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

#1835. Jesus Owono’s punishment criticised following death of Jesus de Miguel

Andorra owner Gerard Pique says Jesus Owono ‘does not deserve’ the 12-game suspension he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The footballing world was rocked earlier this month as it was announced that De Miguel had tragically passed away at the age of 30 after he was involved in a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono.

Owono had raced out of goal in the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier contest before clattering into De Miguel, whose severe head and chest injuries caused him to go into cardiac arrest.

It quickly became apparent that De Miguel required urgent medical attention and while the centre-forward’s condition was described as ‘stable but serious’ after he was carried from the field and taken to hospital, his condition quickly deteriorated – and he died the following day.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the days and weeks that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Last week, Owono learned that he would be banned for Andorra’s next 12 matches for the role he played in the deadly collision, with the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee stating that the player had ‘violently struck an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

It went on: ‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge.

The statement added that the ‘nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances’ meant that the ‘maximum sanction’ was ‘justified’.

It was also confirmed that the match involving Andorra and Tenerife – which was called off when the teams were locked at 2-2 deep into stoppage time – would not be replayed.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘This avoids having to resume play from the precise moment at which the tragic incident occurred,’ it read.

Owono’s suspension has received a mixed reaction in Spain, with some feeling it too lenient while others have called for the ‘distressed’ goalkeeper to be given greater support.

According to Andorra owner Pique, the former Barcelona, Manchester United and Spain defender, Owono is ‘not to blame’ for the tragic outcome of the deadly collision.

‘I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve,’ he said in a statement.

‘He is not to blame for all of this having happened.’

Pique pointed to a separate incident earlier this month in Spanish football, when Albacete attacker Jose Corpas accidentally kicked Sabadell’s Quadri Liameed in the head during a second-tier encounter.

‘Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches,’ Pique added.

‘With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?’

Pique, a World Cup winner with Spain in 2010, made it clear that Owono would likely require a significant break away from the game before being able to compete again.

‘Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to play,’ he continued.

‘No sanction is going to bring De Miguel back to us.’

Tenerife’s grieving squad returned to action for the first time since De Miguel’s death against Cueta on Sunday.

Goals from Nacho Gil and Neal Viereck sealed Tenerife a 2-0 victory on an emotional day the club’s Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.
